functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dwrite_multi(size_t count, hid_t dset_id[], hid_t mem_type_id[], hid_t mem_space_id[], hid_t file_space_id[], hid_t dxpl_id, const void *buf[]);
functions.description: Writes to multiple datasets in one call. Arrays of length count specify datasets, memory datatypes, memory selections, file selections, and source buffers. Equivalent to count H5Dwrite calls but may enable optimizations.
requirements: count must equal the lengths of all array parameters (dset_id, mem_type_id, mem_space_id, file_space_id, buf).
Each dset_id[i] must be valid; all datasets must reside in the same HDF5 file and each unique dataset can appear only once.
If called collectively in parallel, each rank must pass exactly the same dataset list/order.
For each i, the number of elements selected in mem_space_id[i] must equal that in file_space_id[i].
Each buf[i] must point to sufficient data for its selection and datatype.
dxpl_id must be a valid transfer property list or H5P_DEFAULT (implied).

functions.name: H5Dwrite_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dwrite_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t dset_id, hid_t mem_type_id, hid_t mem_space_id, hid_t file_space_id, hid_t dxpl_id, const void *buf, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Dwrite that schedules writing buf to dataset dset_id and associates it with event set es_id. First three parameters capture call-site metadata when invoked via wrappers.
requirements: app_file, app_func, app_line are call-site metadata (typically supplied by macro).
All H5Dwrite requirements apply to dset_id, mem_type_id, mem_space_id, file_space_id, dxpl_id, and buf.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Dwrite_multi_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dwrite_multi_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, size_t count, hid_t dset_id[], hid_t mem_type_id[], hid_t mem_space_id[], hid_t file_space_id[], hid_t dxpl_id, const void *buf[], hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Dwrite_multi; schedules writing to multiple datasets and associates the operation set with es_id. First three parameters carry call-site metadata.
requirements: app_file, app_func, app_line are call-site metadata.
All H5Dwrite_multi requirements apply to count and the arrays.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Dwrite_chunk
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dwrite_chunk(hid_t dset_id, hid_t dxpl_id, uint32_t filters, const hsize_t *offset, size_t data_size, const void *buf);
functions.description: Writes a single raw data chunk directly to a chunked dataset at logical chunk offset, bypassing the standard I/O pipeline and filters. The filters mask records which filters were applied/skipped; data_size specifies bytes to write (e.g., compressed size).
requirements: dset_id must refer to a chunked dataset; function is not supported with parallel HDF5 and does not support variable-length types.
filters is a bitmask; bit set at a filter’s pipeline position indicates that filter was skipped; zero means all enabled filters applied.
offset must point to an array of length equal to dataset rank; values must be within extent and lie on chunk boundaries.
data_size must be the size in bytes of the chunk being written (on-disk size if precompressed).
buf must point to at least data_size bytes.
dxpl_id must be a valid transfer property list or H5P_DEFAULT (implied).
Use with caution: bypasses hyperslab selection, datatype conversion, and filter pipeline.

functions.name: H5Dread_chunk2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dread_chunk2(hid_t dset_id, hid_t dxpl_id, const hsize_t *offset, uint32_t *filters, void *buf, size_t *buf_size);
functions.description: Reads a single raw data chunk directly from a chunked dataset at logical chunk offset into buf, bypassing the standard I/O pipeline and filters. On input, *buf_size is the allocated size of buf; on return, *buf_size is set to the required size (the on-disk chunk size). If the provided buffer is too small, no data is read; filters is always set to the chunk’s filter mask.
requirements: dset_id must refer to a chunked dataset; function is not supported with parallel HDF5 and does not support variable-length datatypes.
offset must point to an array (length = dataset rank) specifying the chunk origin (on a chunk boundary and within extent).
filters must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the filter mask.
buf may be NULL only if *buf_size is 0; otherwise buf must point to at least *buf_size bytes.
buf_size must be a non-NULL pointer; on entry, *buf_size is the allocated size; on exit, set to required size (whether or not read succeeded).
dxpl_id must be a valid transfer property list or H5P_DEFAULT (implied).
Use with caution: bypasses hyperslab selection and datatype conversion.

functions.name: H5Diterate
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Diterate(void *buf, hid_t type_id, hid_t space_id, H5D_operator_t op, void *operator_data);
functions.description: Iterates over all elements selected in dataspace space_id within the memory buffer buf, invoking callback op once per element. Cannot be resumed from an intermediate point; changing space_id’s selection during iteration yields undefined behavior.
requirements: buf must point to memory containing elements laid out per space_id and type_id.
type_id must be a valid datatype describing elements in buf.
space_id must be a valid dataspace with a defined selection; do not modify its selection during iteration.
op must be a valid callback; its return value controls iteration (non-zero stops, negative signals error).
operator_data is passed through to the callback and may be NULL.

functions.name: H5Dvlen_get_buf_size
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dvlen_get_buf_size(hid_t dset_id, hid_t type_id, hid_t space_id, hsize_t *size);
functions.description: Determines the number of bytes required to store variable-length (VL) data from dataset dset_id for the selection space_id when represented in memory as type_id. Returns the required size in *size.
requirements: dset_id must be valid.
type_id must be a valid datatype describing memory representation of the VL data.
space_id must be a valid dataspace defining the selection in the dataset on disk.
size must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the required bytes.

functions.name: H5Dfill
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dfill(const void *fill, hid_t fill_type_id, void *buf, hid_t buf_type_id, hid_t space_id);
functions.description: Fills the selection defined by space_id in the memory buffer buf with the given fill value. If fill is NULL, uses a zero fill. If fill_type_id differs from buf_type_id, the fill value is converted before writing.
requirements: fill may be NULL (treated as zero value) or point to a value of type fill_type_id.
fill_type_id must be a valid datatype for the fill value.
buf must point to a buffer whose selected elements (per space_id) will be written.
buf_type_id must be a valid datatype describing elements in buf.
space_id must be a valid dataspace describing the memory buffer’s extent and selection.

functions.name: H5Dset_extent
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dset_extent(hid_t dset_id, const hsize_t size[]);
functions.description: Changes the current dimensions of a dataset to the sizes specified in size. Applicable to chunked datasets (and external datasets with constraints). May allocate space and/or write fill values depending on allocation and fill-time properties. Reducing dimensions can discard data; caller is responsible.
requirements: dset_id must be a valid dataset identifier; generally requires chunked storage except for external datasets.
size must point to an array with length equal to the dataset’s rank; values specify new current sizes (must be within maxdims).
If reducing dimensions, application is responsible for not losing needed data; function does not validate content safety.
After changing extent, any previously obtained dataspace handles become stale; caller should close and reacquire via H5Dget_space().

functions.name: H5Dset_extent_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dset_extent_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t dset_id, const hsize_t size[], hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Dset_extent that schedules an extent change associated with event set es_id. The first three parameters capture call-site metadata when using the wrapper macro.
requirements: app_file, app_func, app_line are call-site metadata (typically provided by macro).
All H5Dset_extent requirements on dset_id and size apply.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Dflush
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dflush(hid_t dset_id);
functions.description: Flushes all buffers associated with dataset dset_id to disk without evicting them from the cache. Note: the OS ultimately controls persistence to disk.
requirements: dset_id must be a valid open dataset identifier.

functions.name: H5Drefresh
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Drefresh(hid_t dset_id);
functions.description: Refreshes dataset dset_id by clearing cached metadata and reloading from disk; effectively closes and reopens the dataset under the same identifier.
requirements: dset_id must be a valid open dataset identifier.

functions.name: H5Dscatter
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dscatter(H5D_scatter_func_t op, void *op_data, hid_t type_id, hid_t dst_space_id, void *dst_buf);
functions.description: Scatters data into the selection defined by dst_space_id within dst_buf by repeatedly invoking callback op to obtain chunks of source data. The datatype type_id applies to both source and destination.
requirements: op must be a valid callback that returns a source buffer and the number of bytes via its protocol; it must not return more elements than remain.
op_data is passed through to the callback; may be NULL.
type_id must be a valid datatype describing elements in both source and destination.
dst_space_id must be a valid dataspace describing the destination buffer’s extent and selection.
dst_buf must point to at least (number of elements in dst_space extent) * sizeof(type_id) bytes.

functions.name: H5Dgather
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dgather(hid_t src_space_id, const void *src_buf, hid_t type_id, size_t dst_buf_size, void *dst_buf, H5D_gather_func_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: Gathers data from the selection defined by src_space_id within src_buf into a contiguous destination buffer dst_buf, optionally invoking callback op to process data in chunks up to dst_buf_size bytes.
requirements: src_space_id must be a valid dataspace describing the source buffer’s dimensions and selection.
src_buf must point to at least the size of the gathered data (elements in selection × sizeof(type_id)).
type_id must be a valid datatype describing the element size.
dst_buf_size specifies the capacity in bytes of dst_buf for each gather step.
dst_buf must point to sufficient memory if op is NULL; otherwise may be a working buffer reused per callback.
If op is provided, it must process the data in dst_buf before return; it should return 0 for success or negative for failure.
op_data is passed through to the callback and may be NULL.

functions.name: H5Dclose
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dclose(hid_t dset_id);
functions.description: Closes the dataset identified by dset_id and releases associated resources.
requirements: dset_id must be a valid open dataset identifier not already closed.
After successful close, dset_id must not be used.

functions.name: H5Dclose_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dclose_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t dset_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Dclose that schedules closing dataset dset_id associated with event set es_id. First three parameters carry call-site metadata via wrappers.
requirements: app_file, app_func, app_line are call-site metadata (typically provided by macro).
dset_id must be a valid dataset identifier.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Dcreate1
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Dcreate1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t type_id, hid_t space_id, hid_t dcpl_id);
functions.description: Deprecated dataset creation function (superseded by H5Dcreate2). Creates a dataset named name at loc_id with datatype type_id, dataspace space_id, and creation property list dcpl_id.
requirements: Same general requirements as H5Dcreate2 regarding loc_id, name, type_id, space_id, and dcpl_id consistency.
Intermediate groups named in name must already exist (no lcpl to create them).
Caller must close the returned dataset identifier with H5Dclose().

functions.name: H5Dopen1
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Dopen1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name);
functions.description: Deprecated dataset open function (superseded by H5Dopen2). Opens an existing dataset identified by name relative to loc_id.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location (file, group, dataset, named datatype, or attribute).
name must identify an existing dataset.
Caller must close the returned dataset identifier with H5Dclose().

functions.name: H5Dextend
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dextend(hid_t dset_id, const hsize_t size[]);
functions.description: Deprecated function (use H5Dset_extent). Ensures the dataset has at least the sizes specified in size, extending as needed; cannot reduce dimensions. Allocation and fill behavior follow dataset properties.
requirements: dset_id must be valid; dataset must support extension per its maxdims (unlimited or within max).
size must point to an array length equal to dataset rank with new minimum sizes.
May allocate space and write fill values depending on properties; does not reduce dimensions.

functions.name: H5Dvlen_reclaim
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dvlen_reclaim(hid_t type_id, hid_t space_id, hid_t dxpl_id, void *buf);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Treclaim(). Reclaims memory allocated for variable-length (VL) datatype data in buf corresponding to the selection space_id and datatype type_id. Modifies VL structures in buf to clear them; handles nested VL types safely.
requirements: type_id must be the datatype of the data stored in buf (including any nested VL components).
space_id must describe the selection in memory for which VL data should be reclaimed.
dxpl_id must be the dataset transfer property list used for the I/O that created the buffer.
buf must point to the buffer whose VL allocations are to be reclaimed.

functions.name: H5Dread_chunk1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Dread_chunk1(hid_t dset_id, hid_t dxpl_id, const hsize_t *offset, uint32_t *filters, void *buf);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Dread_chunk2 due to potential buffer overflows. Reads a raw data chunk directly from a chunked dataset at logical chunk offset into buf, bypassing the standard I/O pipeline and filters. Sets filters to the filter mask used when the chunk was written.
requirements: dset_id must refer to a chunked dataset; not supported with parallel HDF5 and does not support variable-length datatypes.
offset must point to an array (length = dataset rank) specifying the chunk origin (on chunk boundary and within extent).
filters must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the filter mask.

buf must point to a buffer large enough to hold the entire on-disk chunk; since the size is unknown to the library in this API, caller must ensure sufficient capacity (risk of overflow; recommended to use H5Dread_chunk2).
dxpl_id must be a valid transfer property list or H5P_DEFAULT (implied).

functions.name: H5Eregister_class
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Eregister_class(const char *cls_name, const char *lib_name, const char *version);
functions.description: Registers a client library or application with the HDF5 error API and returns a new error class ID for defining error messages. Typical use is to create a class before creating major/minor messages so errors from that component can be reported with class/library/version preamble. The version string may be NULL.
requirements: cls_name must be a valid, null-terminated string.
lib_name must be a valid, null-terminated string.
version may be NULL or a valid, null-terminated string.
Caller must close the returned class ID when no longer needed (via H5Eunregister_class or other proper close routines).
Returns H5I_INVALID_ID on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eunregister_class
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eunregister_class(hid_t class_id);
functions.description: Removes (unregisters) an error class identified by class_id; all major and minor messages in the class are closed.
requirements: class_id must be a valid error class identifier returned by H5Eregister_class (not H5I_INVALID_ID).
On success, associated major/minor messages are also closed; they must not be used afterward.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eclose_msg
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eclose_msg(hid_t err_id);
functions.description: Closes an error message handle (major or minor). Use after H5Ecreate_msg or when done with a message ID.
requirements: err_id must be a valid error message identifier (major or minor).
After successful close, err_id becomes invalid and must not be reused.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Ecreate_msg
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Ecreate_msg(hid_t cls, H5E_type_t msg_type, const char *msg);
functions.description: Adds (creates) a major or minor error message within an error class and returns its message ID. Close the returned ID with H5Eclose_msg when done.
requirements: cls must be a valid error class ID.
msg_type must be H5E_MAJOR or H5E_MINOR.
msg must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Caller must close the returned message ID with H5Eclose_msg.
Returns H5I_INVALID_HID on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Ecreate_stack
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Ecreate_stack(void);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new, empty error stack. Close the stack with H5Eclose_stack when done.
requirements: Caller must close the returned stack ID with H5Eclose_stack.
Returns H5I_INVALID_ID on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eget_current_stack
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Eget_current_stack(void);
functions.description: Returns a new error stack that is a copy of the current error stack. Close the returned stack with H5Eclose_stack.
requirements: Caller must close the returned stack ID with H5Eclose_stack.
Returns H5I_INVALID_ID on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eappend_stack
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eappend_stack(hid_t dst_stack_id, hid_t src_stack_id, bool close_source_stack);
functions.description: Appends all messages from src_stack_id onto dst_stack_id. Optionally closes the source stack if close_source_stack is true.
requirements: dst_stack_id must be a valid error stack ID.
src_stack_id must be a valid error stack ID.
If close_source_stack is true and the call succeeds, src_stack_id will be closed and must not be used afterward.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eis_paused
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eis_paused(hid_t stack_id, bool *is_paused);
functions.description: Checks whether pushing errors onto the given error stack is currently paused. Intended for VOL connectors and dynamically loaded components.
requirements: stack_id must be a valid error stack ID (can be H5E_DEFAULT to query the default/current stack as applicable).
is_paused must be a non-NULL pointer to a bool; on error, its value is unchanged.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Epause_stack
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Epause_stack(hid_t stack_id);
functions.description: Pauses pushing errors on the specified error stack. Pushing errors while paused is ignored. Calls to pause/resume must be matched and may be nested.
requirements: stack_id must be a valid error stack ID (can be H5E_DEFAULT for the current/default stack).
Each successful H5Epause_stack call must be matched by a corresponding H5Eresume_stack call; nesting is allowed.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eresume_stack
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eresume_stack(hid_t stack_id);
functions.description: Resumes pushing errors on the specified error stack previously paused via H5Epause_stack. Calls must be matched; nesting is allowed.
requirements: stack_id must be a valid error stack ID (can be H5E_DEFAULT for the current/default stack).
Must be called to match a prior successful H5Epause_stack; nested pause levels are supported.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eclose_stack
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eclose_stack(hid_t stack_id);
functions.description: Closes an error stack handle and releases its resources. H5E_DEFAULT cannot be closed.
requirements: stack_id must be a valid error stack ID and not H5E_DEFAULT.
After successful close, stack_id must not be used.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eget_class_name
functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Eget_class_name(hid_t class_id, char *name, size_t size);
functions.description: Retrieves the name of an error class into a user buffer and returns the full length of the class name. If name is NULL or size is 0, only the length is returned.
requirements: class_id must be a valid error class ID.
If name is non-NULL and size > 0, name must point to a buffer of at least size bytes; at most size characters are written.
Returns non-negative on success; negative on failure. If return is 0, the class has no name.
Caller should use the return value to detect truncation and to size buffers appropriately.

functions.name: H5Eset_current_stack
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eset_current_stack(hid_t err_stack_id);
functions.description: Replaces the current error stack with a copy of the specified stack and closes the specified stack.
requirements: err_stack_id must be a valid error stack ID (e.g., from H5Ecreate_stack or H5Eget_current_stack).
On success, err_stack_id is closed and must not be used afterward.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Epush2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Epush2(hid_t err_stack, const char *file, const char *func, unsigned line, hid_t cls_id, hid_t maj_id, hid_t min_id, const char *msg, ...);
functions.description: Pushes a new error record onto the specified error stack (or the current stack if err_stack is H5E_DEFAULT). The record includes file, func, line, error class ID, major/minor message IDs, and a printf-style message.
requirements: err_stack must be a valid error stack ID or H5E_DEFAULT (to use the current stack).
cls_id, maj_id, and min_id must be valid and the major/minor messages must belong to the same error class.
file, func, and msg strings must be statically allocated (per documentation).
line should be the source code line number where the error occurred.
If msg includes format specifiers, corresponding variadic arguments must match the format.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Epop
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Epop(hid_t err_stack, size_t count);
functions.description: Deletes count error records from the top of the specified error stack.
requirements: err_stack must be a valid error stack ID.
count specifies how many records to remove from the top; behavior for count greater than stack depth is not specified here.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eprint2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eprint2(hid_t err_stack, FILE *stream);
functions.description: Prints the specified error stack to the given stream using the default formatting. If err_stack is H5E_DEFAULT, prints the current stack. If stream is NULL, prints to stderr.
requirements: err_stack must be a valid error stack ID or H5E_DEFAULT.
stream may be NULL to indicate stderr, or a valid FILE*.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Ewalk2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ewalk2(hid_t err_stack, H5E_direction_t direction, H5E_walk2_t func, void *client_data);
functions.description: Walks the specified (or current if H5E_DEFAULT) error stack and invokes the callback for each error in either upward or downward order.
requirements: err_stack must be a valid error stack ID or H5E_DEFAULT.
direction must be H5E_WALK_UPWARD or H5E_WALK_DOWNWARD.
func must be a non-NULL callback matching H5E_walk2_t.
client_data is passed through unmodified to the callback.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eget_auto2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eget_auto2(hid_t estack_id, H5E_auto2_t *func, void **client_data);
functions.description: Retrieves the automatic error stack traversal function and its client data for the specified error stack.
requirements: estack_id must be a valid error stack ID (H5E_DEFAULT indicates the current stack).
func may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the current auto function pointer.
client_data may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the current client data pointer.
Do not mix v1 and v2 auto functions as described; mixing set/get styles can cause failure.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eset_auto2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eset_auto2(hid_t estack_id, H5E_auto2_t func, void *client_data);
functions.description: Enables or disables automatic error printing for the specified stack. If func is non-NULL, it is called automatically on error with client_data. If func is NULL, automatic printing is disabled. Default auto function is H5Eprint2 with stderr.
requirements: estack_id must be a valid error stack ID (H5E_DEFAULT indicates the current stack).
func may be NULL to disable automatic printing, or a valid function matching H5E_auto2_t.
client_data is an opaque pointer passed to func when invoked.
Automatic traversal direction is always H5E_WALK_DOWNWARD.
Mixing v1/v2 auto set/get routines (H5Eset_auto1 with H5Eget_auto2, etc.) causes failure.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eclear2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eclear2(hid_t err_stack);
functions.description: Clears all records from the specified error stack, or the current thread’s stack if err_stack is H5E_DEFAULT.
requirements: err_stack must be a valid error stack ID or H5E_DEFAULT.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eauto_is_v2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eauto_is_v2(hid_t err_stack, unsigned *is_stack);
functions.description: Indicates whether the error stack’s auto reporting function conforms to the H5E_auto2_t (v2) or H5E_auto1_t (v1) prototype. Sets *is_stack to 1 for v2, 0 for v1.
requirements: err_stack must be a valid error stack ID.
is_stack must be a non-NULL pointer to unsigned for the result.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eget_msg
functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Eget_msg(hid_t msg_id, H5E_type_t *type, char *msg, size_t size);
functions.description: Retrieves an error message’s text and type given its message ID. Returns the full message length in bytes. If msg is NULL or size is 0, only the length and type are returned.
requirements: msg_id must be a valid error message ID.
type may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives H5E_MAJOR or H5E_MINOR.
If msg is non-NULL and size > 0, msg must point to a buffer of at least size bytes; up to size characters are written.
Return value is the message length; negative indicates failure; zero indicates no message.

functions.name: H5Eget_num
functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Eget_num(hid_t error_stack_id);
functions.description: Returns the number of error records currently stored in the specified error stack.
requirements: error_stack_id must be a valid error stack ID.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.

functions.name: H5Eclear1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eclear1(void);
functions.description: Deprecated. Clears the current thread’s error stack (old API, renamed from H5Eclear).
requirements: No arguments; operates on the current thread’s stack.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.
Use H5Eclear2 for the current API.

functions.name: H5Eget_auto1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eget_auto1(H5E_auto1_t *func, void **client_data);
functions.description: Deprecated. Retrieves the old-style automatic error traversal function (H5E_auto1_t) and its client data for the current stack.
requirements: func may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives the v1 auto function.
client_data may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives client data.
Mixing v1/v2 auto set/get routines can cause failures as documented.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.
Use H5Eget_auto2 for the current API.

functions.name: H5Epush1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Epush1(const char *file, const char *func, unsigned line, H5E_major_t maj, H5E_minor_t min, const char *str);
functions.description: Deprecated. Pushes a new error record onto the current thread’s error stack with major/minor numbers, file, func, line, and a static description string.
requirements: file, func, and str must be statically allocated strings (per documentation).
maj and min must be valid major/minor error identifiers.
line should reflect the source line where the error occurred.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.
Use H5Epush2 with explicit stack and class/message IDs for the current API.

functions.name: H5Eprint1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eprint1(FILE *stream);
functions.description: Deprecated. Prints the current thread’s error stack to stream (or stderr if stream is NULL) using the old default formatting.
requirements: stream may be NULL to indicate stderr, or a valid FILE*.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.
Use H5Eprint2 for the current API.

functions.name: H5Eset_auto1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Eset_auto1(H5E_auto1_t func, void *client_data);
functions.description: Deprecated. Turns old-style automatic error printing on or off for the current stack. If func is non-NULL, it is called automatically with client_data; if NULL, auto printing is disabled.
requirements: func may be NULL (disables auto printing) or a valid function matching H5E_auto1_t.
client_data is an opaque pointer passed to func when invoked.
Automatic traversal direction is H5E_WALK_DOWNWARD.
Mixing v1/v2 auto set/get routines can cause failures as documented.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.
Use H5Eset_auto2 for the current API.

functions.name: H5Ewalk1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ewalk1(H5E_direction_t direction, H5E_walk1_t func, void *client_data);
functions.description: Deprecated. Walks the current thread’s error stack and calls the old-style callback for each record in the specified direction.
requirements: direction must be H5E_WALK_UPWARD or H5E_WALK_DOWNWARD.
func must be a non-NULL callback matching H5E_walk1_t.
client_data is passed to the callback.
Returns negative on failure; caller must check return value.
Use H5Ewalk2 for the current API.

functions.name: H5Eget_major
functions.signature: H5_DLL char *H5Eget_major(H5E_major_t maj);
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns a dynamically allocated string describing the given major error number. Caller must free the returned string.
requirements: maj must be a valid major error number.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check return value.
Caller must free the returned char* to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: H5Eget_minor
functions.signature: H5_DLL char *H5Eget_minor(H5E_minor_t min);
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns a dynamically allocated string describing the given minor error number. Caller must free the returned string. Note: behavior differs from 1.6.x (dynamic allocation in 1.8.x+).
requirements: min must be a valid minor error number.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check return value.
Caller must free the returned char* to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: H5Fis_accessible
functions.signature: htri_t H5Fis_accessible(const char *container_name, hid_t fapl_id);
functions.description: Checks whether the file or container named by container_name can be opened using the given file access property list (FAPL). Use to verify accessibility with a specific VOL/VFD setup before opening. Returns positive if accessible, 0 if not, negative on error.
requirements: container_name must be a valid, NUL-terminated filename or container URI expected by the active VOL/VFD.
fapl_id must be a valid file access property list ID or H5P_DEFAULT.
This function does not open the file; it only tests accessibility using the FAPL.

functions.name: H5Fcreate
functions.signature: hid_t H5Fcreate(const char *filename, unsigned flags, hid_t fcpl_id, hid_t fapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a new HDF5 file and returns a file identifier. Flags must specify creation behavior (truncate or exclusive). File is always created read-write. Use fcpl_id/fapl_id to control creation and access properties.
requirements: filename must be a valid path; if using Unicode paths, follow platform-specific rules.
flags must include exactly one of H5F_ACC_TRUNC or H5F_ACC_EXCL; H5F_ACC_RDWR/H5F_ACC_RDONLY are ignored for create.
If the target file is already open elsewhere, behavior may depend on detection; avoid creating a file already opened.
fcpl_id must be a file creation property list or H5P_DEFAULT.
fapl_id must be a file access property list or H5P_DEFAULT.
Caller must close the returned file ID with H5Fclose().

functions.name: H5Fcreate_async
functions.signature: hid_t H5Fcreate_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, const char *filename, unsigned flags, hid_t fcpl_id, hid_t fapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Fcreate. Schedules file creation on an event set and returns immediately. The app_file/app_func/app_line parameters are automatically supplied via the provided wrapper macro to record call-site info.
requirements: es_id must be a valid event set identifier when using async VOL/connectors.
filename/flags/fcpl_id/fapl_id have the same requirements as H5Fcreate.
Do not pass explicit literals for app_file/app_func/app_line when using the provided wrapper macro; call H5Fcreate_async(...) normally so the macro supplies them.
Caller must close the resulting file ID with H5Fclose() when creation completes successfully.

functions.name: H5Fopen
functions.signature: hid_t H5Fopen(const char *filename, unsigned flags, hid_t fapl_id);
functions.description: Opens an existing HDF5 file and returns a file identifier. Use flags to select read-only/read-write and optional SWMR modes. Access properties come from fapl_id.
requirements: filename must refer to an existing file or container supported by the active VOL/VFD.
flags must include exactly one of H5F_ACC_RDONLY or H5F_ACC_RDWR; SWMR requires combining with H5F_ACC_SWMR_READ (with RDONLY) or H5F_ACC_SWMR_WRITE (with RDWR).
fapl_id must be a valid file access property list ID or H5P_DEFAULT.
Multiple opens of the same file may require identical flags and compatible fclose degree to avoid errors; avoid multiple opens on files where detection is unreliable.
Caller must close the returned file ID with H5Fclose().

functions.name: H5Fopen_async
functions.signature: hid_t H5Fopen_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, const char *filename, unsigned flags, hid_t access_plist, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Fopen. Schedules file open on an event set. app_file/app_func/app_line are call-site metadata supplied by the wrapper macro.
requirements: filename/flags/access_plist have the same constraints as H5Fopen.
es_id must be a valid event set ID in an async-enabled build/connector.
Use via the provided macro so app_file/app_func/app_line are auto-filled.
Caller must close the returned file ID with H5Fclose() after successful open.

functions.name: H5Freopen
functions.signature: hid_t H5Freopen(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Returns a new file identifier referring to the same open file as file_id. Shares caches with the original, but is not mounted anywhere.
requirements: file_id must be a valid, currently open file identifier.
This does not reopen a closed file; file_id must remain valid at call time.
Caller must close the returned file identifier with H5Fclose().

functions.name: H5Freopen_async
functions.signature: hid_t H5Freopen_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t file_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Freopen. Schedules duplication of a file ID on an event set. Call-site info provided by macro parameters.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
es_id must be a valid event set ID in async-enabled environments.
Use via the macro wrapper to auto-supply app_file/app_func/app_line.
Caller must close the returned file identifier with H5Fclose().

functions.name: H5Fflush
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fflush(hid_t object_id, H5F_scope_t scope);
functions.description: Flushes all HDF5 buffers associated with the file containing object_id to storage, without evicting cached data. Scope controls local vs. global across mount hierarchy.
requirements: object_id must be a valid ID for any object associated with the target file (file, group, dataset, attribute, or named datatype).
scope must be H5F_SCOPE_LOCAL or H5F_SCOPE_GLOBAL.
Actual persistence depends on OS buffering; HDF5 requests OS flush but cannot guarantee physical media write.

functions.name: H5Fflush_async
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fflush_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t object_id, H5F_scope_t scope, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Fflush. Schedules a flush on an event set. app_file/app_func/app_line carry call-site information.
requirements: object_id and scope have the same requirements as H5Fflush.
es_id must be a valid event set ID.
Use via the macro wrapper to auto-supply app_file/app_func/app_line.

functions.name: H5Fclose
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fclose(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Terminates access to an HDF5 file, flushing data to storage. If objects within the file remain open, the file close may be delayed (except in environments where delayed close is not possible).
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
All open objects should be closed before calling in environments where delayed close is not supported (e.g., MPI-IO collective semantics, token-based FS).
After successful close, file_id is invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: H5Fclose_async
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fclose_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t file_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Fclose. Schedules a file close operation on an event set. app_* parameters record call-site.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
es_id must be a valid event set ID.
Use via the macro wrapper to auto-fill app_file/app_func/app_line.
Outstanding open objects may delay close as with H5Fclose.

functions.name: H5Fdelete
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fdelete(const char *filename, hid_t fapl_id);
functions.description: Deletes an HDF5 "file" or container using the VOL/VFD semantics described by the given FAPL. Useful for connectors mapping to non-filesystem storage.
requirements: filename must identify the target as interpreted by the active VOL/VFD.
fapl_id must be configured with the same VOL/VFD used to create/open the file (or H5P_DEFAULT when appropriate).
The function first verifies the target is an HDF5 file via H5Fis_accessible(); it is not a general-purpose delete.

functions.name: H5Fget_create_plist
functions.signature: hid_t H5Fget_create_plist(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Returns a copy of the file creation property list used to create the file. Useful to duplicate creation settings for another file.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
The returned property list ID must be closed with H5Pclose().

functions.name: H5Fget_access_plist
functions.signature: hid_t H5Fget_access_plist(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Returns a copy of the file access property list for the specified file.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
The returned property list ID must be closed with H5Pclose().

functions.name: H5Fget_intent
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_intent(hid_t file_id, unsigned *intent);
functions.description: Retrieves the access mode flags (intent) originally used to open the file, including SWMR-related flags in newer versions.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
intent may be NULL (no-op for the output).
Returned flags correspond to those passed to H5Fopen().

functions.name: H5Fget_fileno
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_fileno(hid_t file_id, unsigned long *fileno);
functions.description: Retrieves a file number that uniquely identifies the open file instance when supported by the VFD and filesystem.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
fileno must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number.
Uniqueness is guaranteed only if the VFD implements file comparison and the filesystem can detect multiple opens.

functions.name: H5Fget_obj_count
functions.signature: ssize_t H5Fget_obj_count(hid_t file_id, unsigned types);
functions.description: Returns the number of currently open HDF5 object identifiers of the specified types associated with the given file (or across all files if file_id is H5F_OBJ_ALL).
requirements: file_id must be a valid file identifier or H5F_OBJ_ALL.
types must be a combination of H5F_OBJ_* flags; optionally OR with H5F_OBJ_LOCAL to restrict to objects opened through file_id.
Return value is negative on error; non-negative count otherwise.

functions.name: H5Fget_obj_ids
functions.signature: ssize_t H5Fget_obj_ids(hid_t file_id, unsigned types, size_t max_objs, hid_t *obj_id_list);
functions.description: Writes up to max_objs open object identifiers of the specified types into obj_id_list for the given file (or all files), and returns the number written.
requirements: file_id must be a valid file identifier or H5F_OBJ_ALL.
types must be a combination of H5F_OBJ_* flags (and optional H5F_OBJ_LOCAL).
If obj_id_list is non-NULL, max_objs must be > 0 and obj_id_list must point to a buffer of at least max_objs entries.
To query needed size, first call with obj_id_list == NULL to get the count, then allocate and call again.

functions.name: H5Fget_vfd_handle
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_vfd_handle(hid_t file_id, hid_t fapl, void **file_handle);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the low-level VFD-specific file handle for the open file, as interpreted using the provided FAPL (e.g., family/multi).
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
fapl is typically H5P_DEFAULT; for FAMILY/MULTI VFDs, it must be set appropriately (e.g., H5Pset_family_offset/H5Pset_multi_type).
file_handle must be a non-NULL pointer to a void* storage to receive the VFD handle; the type and lifetime are VFD-specific.

functions.name: H5Fmount
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fmount(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t child, hid_t plist);
functions.description: Mounts an HDF5 file (child) onto a group at path name relative to loc_id, creating a virtual file hierarchy.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location (file/group/dataset/attribute/named datatype) determining the mount point context.
name must be a valid path to a group (or object location) where the child file will be mounted.
child must be a valid open file identifier to be mounted.
plist must be H5P_DEFAULT; no file mount properties are defined.
If loc_id refers to a dataset/named datatype/attribute, the mount point is the location where that object is attached.

functions.name: H5Funmount
functions.signature: herr_t H5Funmount(hid_t loc_id, const char *name);
functions.description: Unmounts a file from the specified mount point (either the parent’s group or the mounted file’s root group). Does not close either file.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location (file/group/dataset/attribute/named datatype).
name must identify the mount point used for the original mount.

functions.name: H5Fget_freespace
functions.signature: hssize_t H5Fget_freespace(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Returns the amount of free (unused) space, in bytes, tracked in the file, depending on the configured free-space strategy.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
Return value is negative on error; otherwise the free space size.

functions.name: H5Fget_filesize
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_filesize(hid_t file_id, hsize_t *size);
functions.description: Retrieves the total size of the file on storage (user block + HDF5 data + any appended data).
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
size must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the size.

functions.name: H5Fget_eoa
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_eoa(hid_t file_id, haddr_t *eoa);
functions.description: Gets the file’s End Of Allocation (EOA) value, i.e., the end-of-file address maintained in the superblock.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
eoa must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the EOA.

functions.name: H5Fincrement_filesize
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fincrement_filesize(hid_t file_id, hsize_t increment);
functions.description: Increases the file’s EOA to max(EOA, EOF) + increment.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
increment is the number of bytes to add; must be a valid size (non-negative by type).

functions.name: H5Fget_file_image
functions.signature: ssize_t H5Fget_file_image(hid_t file_id, void *buf_ptr, size_t buf_len);
functions.description: Copies the current image of the open file into the user buffer and returns the number of bytes copied (or needed). Supports SEC2/STDIO/Core VFDs.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
If buf_ptr is NULL, no data is copied; the return value indicates required buffer size.
If buf_ptr is non-NULL, buf_len must be at least the required size; otherwise the call fails.
Buffer must be writable when provided.

functions.name: H5Fget_mdc_config
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_mdc_config(hid_t file_id, H5AC_cache_config_t *config_ptr);
functions.description: Loads the current metadata cache configuration for the file into config_ptr. Only the version field is an input.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
config_ptr must be non-NULL and must have its version field set appropriately before call; other fields are outputs.

functions.name: H5Fset_mdc_config
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fset_mdc_config(hid_t file_id, const H5AC_cache_config_t *config_ptr);
functions.description: Attempts to configure the file’s metadata cache according to the parameters in config_ptr.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
config_ptr must be non-NULL and point to a properly initialized H5AC_cache_config_t (valid version and fields).
Invalid values may cause the call to fail.

functions.name: H5Fget_mdc_hit_rate
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_mdc_hit_rate(hid_t file_id, double *hit_rate_ptr);
functions.description: Retrieves the metadata cache hit rate (hits / (hits + misses)) since last reset for the specified file.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
hit_rate_ptr must be non-NULL to receive the result; undefined if the call fails.

functions.name: H5Fget_mdc_size
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_mdc_size(hid_t file_id, size_t *max_size_ptr, size_t *min_clean_size_ptr, size_t *cur_size_ptr, int *cur_num_entries_ptr);
functions.description: Retrieves size-related metadata cache statistics (max size, min clean size, current size, and number of entries) for the file. Any output can be NULL to skip.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
Output pointers may be NULL individually to omit that field; otherwise must point to writable storage.
Returned values are undefined if the call fails.

functions.name: H5Freset_mdc_hit_rate_stats
functions.signature: herr_t H5Freset_mdc_hit_rate_stats(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Resets the metadata cache hit-rate counters for the specified file.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
May affect adaptive resize behavior if enabled; use with understanding of metadata cache behavior.

functions.name: H5Fget_name
functions.signature: ssize_t H5Fget_name(hid_t obj_id, char *name, size_t size);
functions.description: Returns the name of the file containing the given object ID into the buffer name (up to size bytes, including NUL). Returns the full name length.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid identifier for an object within a file (file, group, dataset, attribute, named datatype).
If name is non-NULL, size must be at least filename length + 1 to store the NUL terminator; otherwise the name is truncated.
On error, name is unchanged and a negative value is returned.

functions.name: H5Fget_info2
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_info2(hid_t obj_id, H5F_info2_t *file_info);
functions.description: Fills an H5F_info2_t with global file information (superblock, free-space manager, shared object header info) for the file containing obj_id.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid identifier within the target file.
file_info must be a non-NULL pointer to writable H5F_info2_t.

functions.name: H5Fget_metadata_read_retry_info
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_metadata_read_retry_info(hid_t file_id, H5F_retry_info_t *info);
functions.description: Retrieves retry histogram information for checksum-protected metadata reads (used mainly for SWMR and debugging). Allocates arrays for entries with retries; caller must free each non-NULL retries[i].
requirements: file_id must be a valid file identifier.
info must be a non-NULL pointer to H5F_retry_info_t to receive results.
On success, for each i with retries, info->retries[i] points to an allocated nbins-length array; the caller must free each non-NULL info->retries[i].

functions.name: H5Fstart_swmr_write
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fstart_swmr_write(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Activates SWMR writing mode for the open file, performing checks and preparing the file (enable retries, disable accumulator, flush) to ensure safe SWMR operation.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier with write access (H5F_ACC_RDWR).
The file must be opened with the latest library format to ensure checksummed metadata is used.
The file must not already be in SWMR write mode.
Committed datatypes and attributes must not be left open when activating SWMR write mode; groups and datasets may remain open.

functions.name: H5Fget_free_sections
functions.signature: ssize_t H5Fget_free_sections(hid_t file_id, H5F_mem_t type, size_t nsects, H5F_sect_info_t *sect_info);
functions.description: Retrieves information about free-space sections for the specified free-space manager type (or all) in a file. Returns number of sections available or filled.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
type must be a valid H5F_mem_t or H5FD_MEM_DEFAULT to query all.
If sect_info is non-NULL, nsects must be > 0 and sect_info must point to an array with at least nsects entries.
To query the total count without retrieving details, call with sect_info == NULL; the return value is the total number of sections.
Call fails if free-space info cannot be retrieved.

functions.name: H5Fclear_elink_file_cache
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fclear_elink_file_cache(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Clears the external link open file cache for the specified file, potentially closing cached child files if nothing else keeps them open.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
This does not close or disable the cache itself; subsequent traversals may repopulate it.

functions.name: H5Fset_libver_bounds
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fset_libver_bounds(hid_t file_id, H5F_libver_t low, H5F_libver_t high);
functions.description: Sets the version bounds (earliest and latest library format versions) for object creation in the open file.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
low and high must be valid H5F_libver_t values with low <= high by library rules (as defined by H5Pset_libver_bounds semantics).

functions.name: H5Fstart_mdc_logging
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fstart_mdc_logging(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Starts logging metadata cache events for the file if logging support was enabled via the FAPL. Opens/uses the log file and begins recording.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
Metadata cache logging must have been enabled via H5Pset_mdc_log_options() when opening/creating the file; calling when already logging is an error.
Logging can incur significant overhead.

functions.name: H5Fstop_mdc_logging
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fstop_mdc_logging(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Stops metadata cache event logging for the file (if enabled and currently active). Leaves the log file open until the HDF5 file is closed.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
Logging must have been enabled via H5Pset_mdc_log_options().
This suspends logging only; it does not close the log file.

functions.name: H5Fget_mdc_logging_status
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_mdc_logging_status(hid_t file_id, bool *is_enabled, bool *is_currently_logging);
functions.description: Returns whether metadata cache logging is enabled for the file and whether it is currently logging.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
is_enabled and is_currently_logging must be non-NULL pointers to receive flags.

functions.name: H5Freset_page_buffering_stats
functions.signature: herr_t H5Freset_page_buffering_stats(hid_t file_id);
functions.description: Resets page buffer statistics for the specified file.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
Only meaningful when page buffering is enabled for the file.

functions.name: H5Fget_page_buffering_stats
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_page_buffering_stats(hid_t file_id, unsigned accesses[2], unsigned hits[2], unsigned misses[2], unsigned evictions[2], unsigned bypasses[2]);
functions.description: Retrieves page buffer statistics: counts of metadata/raw data accesses, hits, misses, evictions, and bypasses, each reported as a two-element array [metadata, raw].
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
Each output array pointer must be non-NULL and point to space for two unsigned entries.
Only meaningful when page buffering is enabled.

functions.name: H5Fget_mdc_image_info
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_mdc_image_info(hid_t file_id, haddr_t *image_addr, hsize_t *image_size);
functions.description: Reports the offset and length of a metadata cache image in the file if it exists; otherwise returns HADDR_UNDEF and 0. For read/write opens, call immediately after open (before any metadata access) as the image is read and deleted on first use.
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
image_addr and image_size must be non-NULL pointers to receive results.
When opened read/write, must be called immediately after H5Fopen to see existing image; in read-only, may be called anytime.

functions.name: H5Fget_dset_no_attrs_hint
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_dset_no_attrs_hint(hid_t file_id, bool *minimize);
functions.description: Retrieves the per-file flag indicating whether the library should create minimized dataset object headers (expecting no attributes).
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
minimize must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the flag.

functions.name: H5Fset_dset_no_attrs_hint
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fset_dset_no_attrs_hint(hid_t file_id, bool minimize);
functions.description: Sets the per-file hint to create minimized dataset object headers. Affects all handles referring to the same file-on-disk; interacts with H5Pset_dset_no_attrs_hint().
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
Setting to true hints that datasets will have no attributes; attributes can still be added but may incur performance costs (continuation messages).

functions.name: H5Fset_mpi_atomicity
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fset_mpi_atomicity(hid_t file_id, bool flag);
functions.description: [Parallel only] Sets MPI atomicity (sequential consistency semantics) for MPI-IO operations on the file. Collective call; may significantly impact performance.
requirements: Available only when the library is built with parallel support (HDF5_ENABLE_PARALLEL) and used with the MPIO VFD.
file_id must be a valid open file identifier opened with the MPIO driver.
All participating MPI processes must call collectively with the same file_id and identical flag.
flag must be 1 (atomic) or 0 (nonatomic).
Underlying platform must support MPI_File_set_atomicity; otherwise unsupported.

functions.name: H5Fget_mpi_atomicity
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_mpi_atomicity(hid_t file_id, bool *flag);
functions.description: [Parallel only] Gets whether MPI atomic file access mode is enabled for the file.
requirements: Available only with parallel-enabled library and MPIO usage.
file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
flag must be a non-NULL pointer to receive 1 (atomic) or 0 (nonatomic).

functions.name: H5Fget_info1
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fget_info1(hid_t obj_id, H5F_info1_t *file_info);
functions.description: Deprecated: Returns global file information (superblock extension size and shared object header info) for the file containing obj_id. Use H5Fget_info2 instead.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid identifier within the target file.
file_info must be a non-NULL pointer to writable H5F_info1_t.
This API is deprecated; prefer H5Fget_info2.

functions.name: H5Fset_latest_format
functions.signature: herr_t H5Fset_latest_format(hid_t file_id, bool latest_format);
functions.description: Deprecated: Sets whether to use the latest library format for writing objects in the open file. Superseded by H5Fset_libver_bounds().
requirements: file_id must be a valid open file identifier.
latest_format is a boolean toggle.
Deprecated since 1.10.2; prefer H5Fset_libver_bounds().

functions.name: H5Fis_hdf5
functions.signature: htri_t H5Fis_hdf5(const char *file_name);
functions.description: Deprecated: Determines whether the named file is in HDF5 format using default drivers. Prefer H5Fis_accessible() to check accessibility with a specific FAPL.
requirements: file_name must be a valid, NUL-terminated path string.
Uses default file driver only; may not reflect accessibility via custom VOL/VFD.
Returns positive if HDF5, 0 if not, negative on error.

functions.name: H5Gcreate2
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gcreate2(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t gcpl_id, hid_t gapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a new HDF5 group and links it into the file at the path name relative to loc_id. Use lcpl_id for link creation properties, gcpl_id for group creation properties, and gapl_id for access properties (H5P_DEFAULT permitted). Returns a group identifier that must be closed with H5Gclose().
requirements: loc_id must be a valid identifier to a location in the file (file, group, dataset, named datatype, or attribute).
name must be a valid absolute or relative path; intermediate groups must exist per the link creation properties used.
lcpl_id, gcpl_id, and gapl_id must be valid property list identifiers or H5P_DEFAULT.
The returned group identifier must be closed with H5Gclose() to avoid resource leaks.

functions.name: H5Gcreate_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gcreate_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t gcpl_id, hid_t gapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Gcreate2. Creates and links a new group, enqueuing the operation on the event set es_id. The app_file/app_func/app_line parameters are filled by wrapper macros for debugging/tracing. Returns a group identifier (the operation completes asynchronously).
requirements: app_file, app_func are non-null strings and app_line is typically a source line number (normally supplied by wrapper macros).
loc_id must be a valid HDF5 location identifier (file, group, dataset, named datatype, or attribute).
name must be a valid group path (absolute or relative).
lcpl_id, gcpl_id, gapl_id must be valid property list IDs or H5P_DEFAULT.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier for asynchronous execution.
The returned group identifier must eventually be closed with H5Gclose().

functions.name: H5Gcreate_anon
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gcreate_anon(hid_t loc_id, hid_t gcpl_id, hid_t gapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a new anonymous (unlinked) group in the file associated with loc_id. The group is not linked into the file structure; link it later with H5Olink() or it will be deleted when the file is closed. Returns a group identifier; close with H5Gclose().
requirements: loc_id must specify the target file via a valid identifier.
gcpl_id and gapl_id must be valid property list identifiers or H5P_DEFAULT.
The created group must be linked into the file (e.g., with H5Olink()) before file close to persist; otherwise it is deleted.
The returned group identifier must be closed with H5Gclose().

functions.name: H5Gopen2
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gopen2(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t gapl_id);
functions.description: Opens an existing group at path name relative to loc_id and returns a group identifier. gapl_id specifies group access properties (H5P_DEFAULT allowed). Close the identifier with H5Gclose().
requirements: loc_id must be a valid identifier serving as the starting location (file, group, dataset, named datatype, or attribute).
name must be the name or path of an existing group (may be absolute or relative to loc_id).
gapl_id must be a valid property list or H5P_DEFAULT.
Close the returned group with H5Gclose().

functions.name: H5Gopen_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gopen_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t gapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Gopen2. Opens an existing group at name relative to loc_id and enqueues the operation on es_id. Wrapper macros provide app_file/app_func/app_line. Returns a group identifier; close with H5Gclose().
requirements: app_file and app_func are non-null strings and app_line is typically a source line number (normally supplied by wrapper macros).
loc_id must be a valid HDF5 starting location identifier.
name must name an existing group (absolute or relative).
gapl_id must be a valid property list or H5P_DEFAULT.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.
Close the returned group with H5Gclose().

functions.name: H5Gget_create_plist
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gget_create_plist(hid_t group_id);
functions.description: Returns an identifier for the group creation property list associated with the given group. The returned property list must be closed with H5Pclose().
requirements: group_id must be a valid open group identifier.
The returned property list identifier must be closed with H5Pclose() to avoid leaks.

functions.name: H5Gget_info
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_info(hid_t loc_id, H5G_info_t *ginfo);
functions.description: Retrieves information (storage_type, nlinks, max_corder, mounted) about the group specified by loc_id and stores it in ginfo.
requirements: loc_id must identify the target group object (valid open group identifier).
ginfo must be a non-null pointer to H5G_info_t storage.

functions.name: H5Gget_info_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_info_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, H5G_info_t *ginfo /*out*/, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Gget_info. Enqueues a request to retrieve group info for the group at loc_id, placing results in ginfo, on the event set es_id. app_file/app_func/app_line are provided by macros for tracing.
requirements: app_file and app_func are non-null strings and app_line is a source line number (normally supplied by wrapper macros).
loc_id must be a valid open group identifier.
ginfo must be a non-null pointer to H5G_info_t for output.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Gget_info_by_name
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_info_by_name(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5G_info_t *ginfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves H5G_info_t for the group named name at or below loc_id. name may be "." if loc_id is the group itself. lapl_id is the link access property list (H5P_DEFAULT allowed).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier serving as the starting point for name resolution.
name must be a valid group name or "." for the group at loc_id.
ginfo must be a non-null pointer to H5G_info_t.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Gget_info_by_name_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_info_by_name_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5G_info_t *ginfo /*out*/, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Gget_info_by_name. Retrieves group info for the group named name at or below loc_id, scheduling on es_id. Wrapper macros fill app_file/app_func/app_line.
requirements: app_file and app_func are non-null strings and app_line is a source line number (normally supplied by wrapper macros).
loc_id must be a valid starting location identifier.
name must name a group (may be ".").
ginfo must be a non-null pointer to H5G_info_t.
lapl_id must be valid or H5P_DEFAULT.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Gget_info_by_idx
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_info_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5G_info_t *ginfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves H5G_info_t for a group identified by its position n within the specified index (idx_type, order) of the group group_name located at or below loc_id. group_name may be "." for loc_id itself.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid starting location identifier.
group_name must be a valid group path or "." for the group at loc_id.
idx_type must be a valid H5_index_t value.
order must be a valid H5_iter_order_t value specifying traversal order.
n selects the position in the index; it must be within the bounds of the chosen index or the call fails.
ginfo must be a non-null pointer to H5G_info_t.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Gget_info_by_idx_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_info_by_idx_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5G_info_t *ginfo /*out*/, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Gget_info_by_idx. Retrieves group info for the group located by index position n within the specified index of group_name at loc_id, queued on es_id. Debug parameters are supplied by macros.
requirements: app_file and app_func are non-null strings and app_line is a source line number (normally supplied by wrapper macros).
loc_id must be valid.
group_name must be a valid group path or ".".
idx_type must be a valid H5_index_t.
order must be a valid H5_iter_order_t.
n must be within the valid range for the selected index or the call fails.
ginfo must be a non-null pointer to H5G_info_t.
lapl_id must be valid or H5P_DEFAULT.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Gflush
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gflush(hid_t group_id);
functions.description: Flushes all buffers associated with the specified group to disk, without evicting cached data. Note that the OS ultimately controls physical flush to media.
requirements: group_id must be a valid open group identifier.

functions.name: H5Grefresh
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Grefresh(hid_t group_id);
functions.description: Clears and reloads all cached metadata and data for the specified group from disk. Effectively closes and reopens the group, preserving the same identifier.
requirements: group_id must be a valid open group identifier.

functions.name: H5Gclose
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gclose(hid_t group_id);
functions.description: Closes an open group identifier previously returned by H5Gcreate* or H5Gopen*. Frees resources; the identifier becomes invalid after close.
requirements: group_id must be a valid open group identifier.
Each open group identifier should be closed exactly once to avoid leaks or invalid reuse.

functions.name: H5Gclose_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gclose_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t group_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Gclose. Enqueues a close of group_id on event set es_id. Debug parameters are provided by wrapper macros.
requirements: app_file and app_func are non-null strings and app_line is a source line number (normally supplied by wrapper macros).
group_id must be a valid open group identifier.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.

functions.name: H5Gcreate1
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gcreate1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, size_t size_hint);
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a new group at name relative to loc_id using default properties. size_hint is a hint for the number of bytes to reserve for names. Returns a group identifier to be closed with H5Gclose().
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier (file, group, dataset, named datatype, or attribute).
name must not already exist; all parent groups must already exist.
size_hint must be between 0 and UINT32_MAX inclusive; if 0, a default is used.
The returned group identifier must be closed with H5Gclose().

functions.name: H5Gopen1
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Gopen1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name);
functions.description: Deprecated. Opens an existing group name relative to loc_id and returns a group identifier. Close with H5Gclose().
requirements: loc_id must be a valid starting location identifier.
name must name an existing group.
Close the returned group with H5Gclose().

functions.name: H5Glink
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Glink(hid_t cur_loc_id, H5G_link_t type, const char *cur_name, const char *new_name);
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a new link of the specified type from new_name to cur_name, both interpreted relative to cur_loc_id for hard links; for soft links, cur_name is stored and resolved relative to the group containing new_name at lookup time.
requirements: cur_loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
type must be H5G_LINK_HARD or H5G_LINK_SOFT (H5L link types).
For H5G_LINK_HARD, cur_name must be the name of an existing object; both cur_name and new_name are interpreted relative to cur_loc_id.
For H5G_LINK_SOFT, cur_name may be any path string; it is interpreted relative to the group containing the final component of new_name at lookup time.
cur_name and new_name must be non-null strings.

functions.name: H5Glink2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Glink2(hid_t cur_loc_id, const char *cur_name, H5G_link_t type, hid_t new_loc_id, const char *new_name);
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a new link of the specified type from new_name to cur_name. For hard links, cur_name is interpreted relative to cur_loc_id and new_name relative to new_loc_id. For soft links, cur_name is stored and resolved relative to the group containing new_name at lookup time.
requirements: cur_loc_id and new_loc_id must be valid file or group identifiers.
type must be H5G_LINK_HARD or H5G_LINK_SOFT.
For H5G_LINK_HARD, cur_name must name an existing object; cur_name is relative to cur_loc_id and new_name relative to new_loc_id.
For H5G_LINK_SOFT, cur_name may be any path string; it is interpreted relative to the group containing new_name at lookup time.
cur_name and new_name must be non-null strings.

functions.name: H5Gmove
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gmove(hid_t src_loc_id, const char *src_name, const char *dst_name);
functions.description: Deprecated. Renames/moves an object within an HDF5 file: unlinks src_name and links it as dst_name atomically. Both names are interpreted relative to src_loc_id.
requirements: src_loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
src_name and dst_name must be non-null path strings.
Exercise care when moving groups; moving can render data inaccessible if paths become invalid (per documentation warning).

functions.name: H5Gmove2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gmove2(hid_t src_loc_id, const char *src_name, hid_t dst_loc_id, const char *dst_name);
functions.description: Deprecated. Renames/moves an object: src_name is interpreted relative to src_loc_id; the destination name dst_name is interpreted relative to dst_loc_id. The unlink and link are performed atomically.
requirements: src_loc_id and dst_loc_id must be valid file or group identifiers.
src_name and dst_name must be non-null path strings.
Exercise care when moving groups; moving can render data inaccessible.

functions.name: H5Gunlink
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gunlink(hid_t loc_id, const char *name);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Ldelete(). Removes the link name from the group graph and decrements the link count on the target object. When the link count reaches zero and the object is not open, storage is freed.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
name must be a non-null path to the link to unlink, interpreted relative to loc_id.
If any identifiers for the target object remain open, space is not released until they are closed.

functions.name: H5Gget_linkval
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_linkval(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, size_t size, char *buf /*out*/);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Lget_val(). For a symbolic link at name relative to loc_id, returns up to size characters of the link value (the target path) into buf. If size is smaller than the value length, the returned string is not null-terminated. Passing size=0 and buf=NULL can be used to test for a symbolic link.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
name must name a symbolic link relative to loc_id; the call fails if name is not a symbolic link.
buf must point to a buffer of at least size bytes when size>0; may be NULL when size==0 to probe.
Caller must handle the possibility that the returned string is not null-terminated if truncated.

functions.name: H5Gset_comment
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gset_comment(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, const char *comment);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Oset_comment(). Sets or removes the comment for the object specified by name relative to loc_id (or "." for loc_id itself). If comment is NULL or empty, removes the comment. Comments are short, null-terminated ASCII strings and apply to objects with object headers (not links).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid identifier to any object in the file.
name must be a valid name relative to loc_id, an absolute path from '/', or "." when loc_id fully specifies the target.
comment may be NULL or empty to remove the comment; otherwise provide a null-terminated ASCII string.
Target must be an object with an object header (datasets, groups, named datatypes); comments cannot be attached to symbolic links.

functions.name: H5Gget_comment
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Gget_comment(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, size_t bufsize, char *buf);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Oget_comment(). Retrieves the comment for the object specified by name relative to loc_id (or "."). Returns the number of characters in the comment including the null terminator; may be larger than bufsize. If no comment exists, an empty string is returned in buf.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid identifier to any object in the file.
name must be a valid name relative to loc_id, an absolute path, or ".".
buf must point to a buffer of at least bufsize bytes if bufsize>0; may be NULL with bufsize=0 to query required size pattern (implied by return semantics).
Caller must handle that the returned length can exceed bufsize; truncation may occur.

functions.name: H5Giterate
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Giterate(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, int *idx, H5G_iterate_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Literate1(). Iterates over the members of the group at name relative to loc_id, invoking op for each entry. Starts at index *idx (or 0 if idx==NULL) and updates *idx to the next element. Iteration is not recursive; membership must remain unchanged during iteration.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
name must be the path to the group to iterate (relative to loc_id).
op must be a valid callback of type H5G_iterate_t; it receives (group, name, op_data) and must follow the documented return conventions: 0 to continue, >0 for short-circuit success, <0 for failure.
idx may be NULL to start at the first member; if non-NULL, on return it is set to the next position.
Do not add or remove members of the group during iteration; behavior is undefined if membership changes.
The iterator does not recurse into subgroups; callers must implement recursion explicitly if needed.

functions.name: H5Gget_num_objs
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_num_objs(hid_t loc_id, hsize_t *num_objs);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Gget_info(). Returns the number of objects in the group specified by loc_id (or in the root group if loc_id is a file identifier).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid group or file identifier.
num_objs must be a non-null pointer to receive the count.

functions.name: H5Gget_objinfo
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Gget_objinfo(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, bool follow_link, H5G_stat_t *statbuf /*out*/);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Oget_info() and H5Lget_info1(). Returns information about the specified object in statbuf. If the object is a symbolic link and follow_link==0, information describes the link; otherwise describes the target. statbuf may be NULL to test for existence.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier or an object identifier when name is ".".
name must be the object name relative to loc_id, or "." when loc_id already identifies the object.
follow_link controls whether to follow final symbolic links (0 = do not follow).
statbuf may be NULL to test existence; otherwise must be non-null to receive information.

functions.name: H5Gget_objname_by_idx
