functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Gget_objname_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, hsize_t idx, char *name, size_t size);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Lget_name_by_idx(). Returns the name of the object at transient index idx within the group specified by loc_id (or the root group if loc_id is a file). If name is NULL, the function returns the required length. If size <= actual length, the name is truncated to size-1 characters.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid group or file identifier.
idx must be a nonnegative index less than the number of objects in the group (as returned by H5Gget_num_objs()).
If name is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least size bytes; caller must handle possible truncation.
A preliminary call with name==NULL can be used to obtain the required length.

functions.name: H5Gget_objtype_by_idx
functions.signature: H5_DLL H5G_obj_t H5Gget_objtype_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, hsize_t idx);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Oget_info(). Returns the type (H5G_obj_t) of the object at transient index idx in the group specified by loc_id. As of 1.12.0, returns the type of the object that the link points to (not the link type).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid group or file identifier.
idx must be a nonnegative index into the group's transient listing.

functions.name: H5Iregister
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Iregister(H5I_type_t type, const void *object);
functions.description: Registers an application object pointer in the specified HDF5 identifier type and returns a new hid_t for it. Typical use is by subsystems creating IDs for internal objects; the pointer is later retrievable with H5Iobject_verify() and is freed via the type’s free function during type clear/destroy. Returns a negative value on failure.
requirements: type must be a valid, registered identifier type (created via H5Iregister_type2 or legacy H5Iregister_type1).
object must point to a valid, library-managed object whose lifetime is managed according to the ID type’s free function.
Caller must check the return value: a negative hid_t indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Iobject_verify
functions.signature: H5_DLL void *H5Iobject_verify(hid_t id, H5I_type_t type);
functions.description: Verifies that id is of the specified type and, if so, returns the stored object pointer associated with the ID. Does not modify the ID or reference counts. Returns NULL if id is not of the given type or on failure.
requirements: id should be a valid identifier; if it is not of the specified type, NULL is returned.
type must be a valid identifier type.

functions.name: H5Iremove_verify
functions.signature: H5_DLL void *H5Iremove_verify(hid_t id, H5I_type_t type);
functions.description: If id is of the specified type, removes the ID from the type and returns the object pointer previously registered for that ID. Does not deallocate the object; the caller is responsible for freeing it. Returns NULL if id is not of the given type or on failure.
requirements: type must be a valid identifier type.
id must belong to the specified type; otherwise NULL is returned.
The returned object pointer is not freed by this function; the caller must deallocate it to avoid leaks.
Caller must check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: H5Iget_type
functions.signature: H5_DLL H5I_type_t H5Iget_type(hid_t id);
functions.description: Returns the identifier type associated with id, or H5I_BADID if no valid type can be determined or id is invalid. Useful for selecting the correct H5*close routine.
requirements: Caller should not assume id validity from this result alone; use H5Iis_valid() to test validity.
Caller must handle H5I_BADID as an error/unknown-type condition.

functions.name: H5Iget_file_id
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Iget_file_id(hid_t id);
functions.description: Returns a file identifier for the file containing the object identified by id. If the file is still open, returns the existing file ID; otherwise reopens the file and returns a new file ID. The returned file ID must be closed with H5Fclose().
requirements: id must identify an object associated with a file.
The returned file identifier must be released with H5Fclose().
Caller must check for negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5Iget_name
functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Iget_name(hid_t id, char *name, size_t size);
functions.description: Retrieves a name for the object identified by id. Up to size bytes (including the null terminator) are written into name. Returns the length of the object name (in bytes); returns 0 if no name is associated. For attribute IDs, returns the name of the object to which the attribute is attached.
requirements: If providing a buffer, size must be the object name length in bytes plus 1 for the null terminator.
name must point to a buffer of at least size bytes when size > 0.
Caller must check the ssize_t return value for errors (negative) and handle truncation if size is too small (only up to size bytes are written).

functions.name: H5Iinc_ref
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Iinc_ref(hid_t id);
functions.description: Increments the in-memory reference count of the object identified by id and returns the new (non-negative) count. The object is only closed when the count reaches zero via H5Idec_ref() or the object’s close routine.
requirements: id should be a valid identifier for an HDF5 object.
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Idec_ref
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Idec_ref(hid_t id);
functions.description: Decrements the in-memory reference count of the object identified by id and returns the new (non-negative) count. When the count reaches zero, the object is closed.
requirements: id should be a valid identifier for an HDF5 object.
Caller must check the return value; a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Iget_ref
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Iget_ref(hid_t id);
functions.description: Returns the current in-memory reference count of the object identified by id, or a negative value on failure.
requirements: id should be a valid identifier for an HDF5 object.
Caller must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5Iregister_type2
functions.signature: H5_DLL H5I_type_t H5Iregister_type2(unsigned reserved, H5I_free_t free_func);
functions.description: Creates a new identifier type and returns its type ID. Optionally reserves a number of IDs and installs a free function that will be called by H5Iclear_type() and H5Idestroy_type() for each registered object pointer in the type (not called by H5Iremove_verify()). The free function should return 0 on success and -1 on failure.
requirements: reserved is the number of IDs to reserve for the new type (may be 0).
free_func must match H5I_free_t signature: herr_t (*)(void *obj, void **request) and return non-negative (0) on success, negative on failure.
free_func must be safe to call for every object registered in this type; it will be invoked during H5Iclear_type() and H5Idestroy_type().
Caller must check the returned H5I_type_t; negative indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Iclear_type
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Iclear_type(H5I_type_t type, bool force);
functions.description: Deletes all identifiers of the given type. Calls the type’s free function on each identifier’s object pointer, then removes the identifiers from the type. If force is false, only identifiers with reference count equal to 1 are deleted; if true, all identifiers of the type are deleted.
requirements: type must be a registered identifier type.
If force is false, only IDs with reference count == 1 will be deleted; others remain unchanged.
Caller must check the return value (non-negative on success, negative on failure).

functions.name: H5Idestroy_type
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Idestroy_type(H5I_type_t type);
functions.description: Destroys an entire identifier type and all identifiers within it. Invokes the type’s free function on all identifiers and frees all memory used by the type. After destruction, no new identifiers of this type can be registered.
requirements: type must be a registered identifier type to be destroyed.
Caller must check the return value (non-negative on success, negative on failure).

functions.name: H5Iinc_type_ref
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Iinc_type_ref(H5I_type_t type);
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an identifier type and returns the current count. The library uses the count to determine when a type can be destroyed.
requirements: type must be a registered identifier type.
Caller must check the return value; negative indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Idec_type_ref
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Idec_type_ref(H5I_type_t type);
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of an identifier type and returns the current count. When the count reaches zero, the type will be destroyed.
requirements: type must be a registered identifier type.
Caller must check the return value; negative indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Iget_type_ref
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Iget_type_ref(H5I_type_t type);
functions.description: Returns the current reference count of an identifier type, or a negative value on failure.
requirements: type must be a registered identifier type.
Caller must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5Isearch
functions.signature: H5_DLL void *H5Isearch(H5I_type_t type, H5I_search_func_t func, void *key);
functions.description: Searches all IDs within the specified type and applies func(obj_pointer, id, key) to each until func returns non-zero; returns the corresponding object pointer. Returns NULL if no object satisfies the predicate or on failure.
requirements: type must be a registered identifier type.
func must match H5I_search_func_t signature: int (*)(void *obj, hid_t id, void *key); return 0 for non-match and non-zero for match.
key is passed through to func and may be NULL as needed by the predicate.
Caller must check for NULL return indicating failure or no match.

functions.name: H5Iiterate
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Iiterate(H5I_type_t type, H5I_iterate_func_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: Invokes the callback op(id, op_data) for each identifier in the given type. Iteration stops if op returns positive (value is returned), or negative (function returns failure). A return of zero continues iteration.
requirements: type must be a registered identifier type.
op must match H5I_iterate_func_t: herr_t (*)(hid_t id, void *udata).
It is undefined behavior to add or remove members of the identifier type during iteration; callers must not modify membership while iterating.
Caller must check the herr_t return: negative indicates failure; positive is the value returned by op.

functions.name: H5Inmembers
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Inmembers(H5I_type_t type, hsize_t *num_members);
functions.description: Retrieves the number of identifiers currently registered in the given identifier type and stores it in num_members. If the type has no identifiers, does not exist, or has been destroyed, returns 0 in num_members.
requirements: type must be the identifier type to query.
num_members must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the count.
Caller must check the return value (non-negative on success, negative on failure).

functions.name: H5Itype_exists
functions.signature: H5_DLL htri_t H5Itype_exists(H5I_type_t type);
functions.description: Determines whether the given identifier type is registered with the library. Returns positive for true, 0 for false, or negative on failure.
requirements: Caller must interpret htri_t correctly: >0 true, 0 false, <0 failure.

functions.name: H5Iis_valid
functions.signature: H5_DLL htri_t H5Iis_valid(hid_t id);
functions.description: Determines whether id is a valid identifier currently usable to access its target. Returns positive for valid, 0 for invalid, or negative on failure.
requirements: Caller must interpret htri_t correctly: >0 valid, 0 invalid, <0 failure.

functions.name: H5Iregister_type1
functions.signature: H5_DLL H5I_type_t H5Iregister_type1(size_t hash_size, unsigned reserved, H5I_free_t free_func);
functions.description: Deprecated: Creates a new identifier type and returns its type ID. hash_size specified the minimum hash table size (unused in 1.8.13 and later). reserved controls the number of reserved IDs. free_func is called by H5Iclear_type() and H5Idestroy_type() for each ID; not called by H5Iremove_verify(). free_func should return 0 on success and -1 on failure. Use H5Iregister_type2() instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer H5Iregister_type2().
free_func must match H5I_free_t and return 0 on success, -1 on failure.
Caller must check the returned H5I_type_t; negative indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Lmove
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lmove(hid_t src_loc, const char *src_name, hid_t dst_loc, const char *dst_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Moves/renames a link within the same HDF5 file as one atomic operation: removes src_name at src_loc and creates dst_name at dst_loc pointing to the same target. Use lcpl_id to control creation of missing intermediate groups and character set; lapl_id controls traversal behavior and external link settings. Does not change the target object nor invalidate existing open IDs to that object.
requirements: src_loc and dst_loc must be valid file or group identifiers within the same HDF5 file.
src_name and dst_name must be valid, null-terminated path names; interpreted relative to src_loc and dst_loc respectively (absolute if starting with '/').
If creating missing intermediate groups is desired, lcpl_id must have H5Pset_create_intermediate_group configured; other LCPL properties are ignored.
lapl_id may set character encoding, traversal limit (H5Pset_nlinks), and external link prefix (H5Pset_elink_prefix).
Using H5L_SAME_LOC is permitted for either src_loc or dst_loc if they are the same location (but not both).
Exercise caution: moving a link that is the only path to an object can render the object inaccessible.

functions.name: H5Lcopy
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lcopy(hid_t src_loc, const char *src_name, hid_t dst_loc, const char *dst_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Creates an identical copy of an existing link (same target and creation time) at a new name/location. Character encoding for the new link is taken from lcpl_id; other LCPL properties are ignored. For soft links, the target is interpreted relative to the copy’s location. Cannot copy hard links across files.
requirements: src_loc and dst_loc must be valid identifiers; dst_loc may be a file (interpreted at root) or group.
src_name and dst_name must be valid, null-terminated path names; interpreted relative to src_loc and dst_loc respectively.
lcpl_id may specify character encoding and create-intermediate-groups (H5Pset_create_intermediate_group); other LCPL properties are ignored.
lapl_id may configure character encoding, traversal limits, and external link prefix.
Copying a hard link across different files is not supported (use H5Ocopy for cross-file copies).

functions.name: H5Lcreate_hard
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lcreate_hard(hid_t cur_loc, const char *cur_name, hid_t dst_loc, const char *dst_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a new hard link dst_name at dst_loc pointing to an existing object identified by cur_name relative to cur_loc. Hard links affect the link count of the target object. lcpl_id/lapl_id are the link creation/access property lists for the new link.
requirements: cur_loc and dst_loc must be valid file or group identifiers (can be the same; H5L_SAME_LOC may be used for one, not both).

cur_name must name an existing object; dst_name is the new link’s name. Both may be absolute (starting with '/') or relative to their respective loc IDs. The created link name is the last path element; parents must exist unless LCPL allows creation.
lcpl_id and lapl_id must be valid identifiers; LCPL can control intermediate group creation; LAPL controls traversal/encoding/prefix.
Hard links are valid only within the same file; for cross-file targets use H5Lcreate_external.
Removing all hard links to an object will delete the object when no identifiers are open.

functions.name: H5Lcreate_hard_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lcreate_hard_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t cur_loc_id, const char *cur_name, hid_t new_loc_id, const char *new_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Lcreate_hard that schedules creation of a hard link on an event set. The app_file/app_func/app_line provide call-site metadata in this wrapper form.
requirements: cur_loc_id and new_loc_id must be valid HDF5 identifiers in the same file.
cur_name must refer to an existing object; new_name is the new link name (path rules as in H5Lcreate_hard).
lcpl_id/lapl_id must be valid property list IDs as for H5Lcreate_hard.
es_id must be a valid event set for async operations.
Hard links cannot cross files; use H5Lcreate_external for cross-file references.
This async wrapper form is available when H5_DOXYGEN is not defined; call-site macros may auto-supply app_file/app_func/app_line.

functions.name: H5Lcreate_soft
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lcreate_soft(const char *link_target, hid_t link_loc_id, const char *link_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a soft (symbolic) link named link_name at link_loc_id whose value is link_target (an HDF5 path string). Target is interpreted at lookup time; may be absolute in the file or relative to link_loc_id. lcpl_id/lapl_id control link creation/access behavior.
requirements: link_target must be a valid, null-terminated HDF5 path string; it may refer to an object that does not exist at creation time (dangling allowed).
link_loc_id must be a valid group or file identifier; if file, link is relative to the root group.
link_name must be a valid, null-terminated path; absolute if starting with '/'. The created link’s name is the last path element; parents must exist unless LCPL allows creation.
lcpl_id and lapl_id must be valid property list identifiers. Soft links are for targets in the same file; for cross-file targets use H5Lcreate_external.

functions.name: H5Lcreate_soft_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lcreate_soft_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, const char *link_target, hid_t link_loc_id, const char *link_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Lcreate_soft that schedules soft link creation on an event set. This wrapper form includes call-site metadata arguments.
requirements: link_target must be a null-terminated path string.
link_loc_id must be a valid location identifier; link_name is a valid path name.
lcpl_id/lapl_id must be valid property lists; es_id must be a valid event set.
For cross-file links, use H5Lcreate_external instead.

functions.name: H5Ldelete
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ldelete(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Removes the link named name from the location loc_id. For hard links, decrements the target object’s link count and may delete the object when the count reaches zero and no IDs remain open.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier (group or file).
name must be a valid, null-terminated path local to loc_id unless absolute; interpreted per lapl_id settings.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list when non-default.
Be cautious: deleting the sole link to an object can render it inaccessible.

functions.name: H5Ldelete_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ldelete_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Ldelete that enqueues link deletion in an event set. Includes call-site metadata.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier; name a valid path string.
lapl_id must be valid if not H5P_DEFAULT; es_id must be a valid event set handle.

functions.name: H5Ldelete_by_idx
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ldelete_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Removes the n-th link from the group specified by loc_id/group_name, using the given index (idx_type) and traversal order (order).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location ID for the parent of group_name.
group_name must identify the subject group; may be "." when loc_id is that group.
idx_type and order must be valid enumeration values for link indexing and ordering.
n is zero-based index of the link to delete within the specified index/order.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list when used.

functions.name: H5Ldelete_by_idx_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ldelete_by_idx_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Ldelete_by_idx that schedules deletion of the n-th link in a group according to the specified index and order. Includes call-site metadata.
requirements: Same as H5Ldelete_by_idx for ids/parameters.
es_id must be a valid event set handle.

functions.name: H5Lget_val
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lget_val(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, void *buf, size_t size, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves the value of a link. For soft links, returns the target path (including null terminator if buffer is large enough). For external or user-defined links, returns their link value buffer. Should be used after determining type/size via H5Lget_info2 or H5Lget_info1. Fails on hard links.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier.
name must be a valid, null-terminated link name/path local to loc_id unless absolute.
buf must point to a buffer of at least size bytes; size should match the link value length obtained from H5Lget_info* (val_size).
If size is smaller than the value length, data is truncated; soft link targets may not be null-terminated.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list if used.
Only call for non-hard links; hard links will cause failure.
For external links, use H5Lunpack_elink_val to parse the returned buffer.

functions.name: H5Lget_val_by_idx
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lget_val_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, void *buf, size_t size, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves the value of the n-th link in a group according to the specified index and order. Soft links yield a path string; external links return an encoded buffer (decode with H5Lunpack_elink_val); user-defined link values depend on their definition. Fails on hard links.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier for the parent of group_name.
group_name specifies the group containing the link; use "." if loc_id is the group.
idx_type and order must be valid enumeration values.
n is zero-based index into the group’s link list per idx_type/order.
buf must be a valid pointer to a buffer of length at least size; size should be obtained from H5Lget_info_by_idx2 (val_size).
lapl_id must be valid if not H5P_DEFAULT.
Only call for non-hard links.

functions.name: H5Lexists
functions.signature: H5_DLL htri_t H5Lexists(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Checks whether a link with the given name exists at the location loc_id. Returns positive on existence, 0 if not, negative on error. In 1.10+, returns positive for name "/" when loc_id is a file or the root group.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
name must be a valid, null-terminated link name or path. Only the final path element is checked; intermediate path elements must exist or the call fails.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list when non-default.
For relative/absolute paths, callers should verify intermediate path components separately to avoid failures as described in the documentation.

functions.name: H5Lexists_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lexists_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, bool *exists, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Lexists. Schedules an existence check; returns result via the boolean pointer exists when the operation completes. Includes call-site metadata.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
name must be a valid path string.
exists must be a non-null pointer to receive the result.
lapl_id must be valid if not H5P_DEFAULT; es_id must be a valid event set handle.

functions.name: H5Lget_info2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lget_info2(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5L_info2_t *linfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Returns metadata about a link name relative to loc_id in an H5L_info2_t struct, including type, creation order info, character set, and either a target token (for hard links) or value size (for soft/UD links).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier.
name must be a valid, null-terminated link name/path (absolute or relative).
linfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to H5L_info2_t storage.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list if used.

functions.name: H5Lget_info_by_idx2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lget_info_by_idx2(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5L_info2_t *linfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Returns H5L_info2_t metadata for the n-th link in the specified group, using the given index and order.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier for the parent of group_name.
group_name specifies the group; may be "." when loc_id is that group.
idx_type and order must be valid enum values; n is a zero-based index.
linfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to H5L_info2_t.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list if used.

functions.name: H5Lget_name_by_idx
functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Lget_name_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, char *name, size_t size, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the n-th link in a group according to the given index and order; returns the size of the link name on success (may be larger than provided buffer).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier for the parent of group_name.
group_name must identify the group; may be "." when loc_id is the group.
idx_type and order must be valid; if H5_ITER_NATIVE is used, order is implementation-defined but consistent.
n is zero-based index; name must be a buffer (may be NULL to query required size).
size specifies the name buffer size; returned value is the full name length even if truncated.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list if used.

functions.name: H5Literate2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Literate2(hid_t grp_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t *idx, H5L_iterate2_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: Iterates over links in a group (non-recursive) in the order specified by idx_type and order, invoking a user callback (H5L_iterate2_t) for each link. The iteration can be resumed via the idx parameter.
requirements: grp_id must be a valid group identifier.
idx_type and order must be valid enumerations; if not pre-indexed, links may be sorted first.
idx may be NULL or a valid pointer to track/resume iteration; if non-NULL, it is both input and output.
op must be a valid callback function pointer; op_data is passed through to the callback.
Behavior is undefined if the group’s link membership changes during iteration.

functions.name: H5Literate_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Literate_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t group_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t *idx_p, H5L_iterate2_t op, void *op_data, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Literate2 that schedules link iteration on an event set; the return value of the callback is not propagated to the API return value.
requirements: group_id must be a valid group ID.
idx_type/order must be valid; idx_p may be NULL or a valid pointer for resume.
op must be a valid callback; op_data is user data passed through.
es_id must be a valid event set; do not rely on API return value to reflect callback’s return.
Group membership must remain unchanged during iteration.

functions.name: H5Literate_by_name2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Literate_by_name2(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t *idx, H5L_iterate2_t op, void *op_data, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Iterates (non-recursive) over links in the named group identified by loc_id/group_name using the specified index and order, invoking a user callback for each link. Supports resuming via idx.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
group_name identifies the group; use "." if loc_id is the group.
idx_type/order must be valid enumerations.
idx may be NULL or a valid pointer to a position; if provided, used for resume.
op must be a valid callback; op_data is passed through.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list if used.
Behavior is undefined if the group’s link membership changes during iteration; iteration is not recursive.

functions.name: H5Lvisit2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lvisit2(hid_t grp_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5L_iterate2_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: Recursively visits all links starting from the group grp_id, traversing in the specified index and order, invoking the callback for each link. Ensures that all links reachable below grp_id are presented unless terminated early by the callback.
requirements: grp_id must be a valid group identifier (or file ID referencing a group).
idx_type/order must be valid; creation-order iteration may fall back to name order for groups not tracked in creation order.
op must be a valid H5L_iterate2_t callback; op_data is passed through.
Callback return values control traversal (0 continue, >0 short-circuit success, <0 failure).

functions.name: H5Lvisit_by_name2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lvisit_by_name2(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5L_iterate2_t op, void *op_data, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Recursively visits all links starting from the named group identified by loc_id/group_name in the specified index and order, invoking a callback per link.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier.
group_name must identify the starting group; may be '.' when loc_id is the group.
idx_type/order must be valid enumerations; creation-order request may fall back to name order where not tracked.
op must be a valid callback; op_data is passed through.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list if used.

functions.name: H5Lcreate_ud
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lcreate_ud(hid_t link_loc_id, const char *link_name, H5L_type_t link_type, const void *udata, size_t udata_size, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a link of a user-defined class link_type named link_name at link_loc_id, storing user-specified opaque data udata of size udata_size. External links (H5L_TYPE_EXTERNAL) are implemented as a UD link class.
requirements: link_loc_id must be a valid location identifier.
link_name must be a valid, null-terminated path; absolute if starting with '/'. Parents must exist unless LCPL allows intermediate group creation.
link_type must be a registered user-defined link class ID (or H5L_TYPE_EXTERNAL). New links of a class require the class to be registered (see H5Lregister).
udata may be NULL only when udata_size is 0; otherwise must point to at least udata_size bytes.
lcpl_id and lapl_id must be valid property list identifiers.

functions.name: H5Lis_registered
functions.signature: H5_DLL htri_t H5Lis_registered(H5L_type_t id);
functions.description: Returns whether a user-defined link class identified by id is currently registered (by the library or via H5Lregister).
requirements: id must be a valid link class identifier to test. Returns >0 if registered, 0 if not, <0 on error.

functions.name: H5Lunpack_elink_val
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lunpack_elink_val(const void *ext_linkval, size_t link_size, unsigned *flags, const char **filename, const char **obj_path);
functions.description: Decodes an external link value buffer (as returned by H5Lget_val for external links) into pointers to the embedded filename and object path strings and returns external link flags (currently none defined; only 0 valid).
requirements: ext_linkval must point to a buffer previously obtained from H5Lget_val for an external link; format is two consecutive null-terminated strings (filename then object path).
link_size is the size in bytes of ext_linkval.
flags may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive a bitmap (currently only 0 is valid).
filename and obj_path may be NULL or valid pointers to receive pointers into the ext_linkval buffer.

Caller must ensure the link is an external link and the buffer format matches; otherwise decoding may fault. Recommended sequence: H5Lget_info* -> verify H5L_TYPE_EXTERNAL -> H5Lget_val -> H5Lunpack_elink_val.

functions.name: H5Lcreate_external
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lcreate_external(const char *file_name, const char *obj_name, hid_t link_loc_id, const char *link_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Creates an external link named link_name at link_loc_id pointing to obj_name in another HDF5 file file_name. Behaves like a soft link; target may not exist at creation. Traversal uses file access properties from H5Pset_elink_fapl and path search rules (env var HDF5_EXT_PREFIX, LAPL prefix, source file path).
requirements: file_name must be a valid path string to the target file (absolute or relative).
obj_name must be an absolute path within the target file (starts at the root of that file).
link_loc_id must be a valid location identifier; link_name is a valid path (absolute if starting with '/'). Parents must exist unless LCPL creates them.
lcpl_id is the link creation property list; lapl_id is the link access property list used for traversal (file close degree is ignored and treated as H5F_CLOSE_WEAK for opened external files).
If additional control over access flags/FAPL is needed, configure via H5Pset_elink_cb/H5Pset_elink_fapl.
External link target file resolution follows the documented search order and stripping rules for absolute paths.

functions.name: H5Lget_info1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lget_info1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5L_info1_t *linfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Lget_info2/H5Lget_info. Returns link metadata in H5L_info1_t (type, creation order info, character set, and either address for hard links or value size for symbolic links).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier.
name must be a valid, null-terminated link name/path.
linfo must be a non-null pointer to H5L_info1_t storage.
lapl_id must be valid if not H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Lget_info_by_idx1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lget_info_by_idx1(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5L_info1_t *linfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Lget_info_by_idx2/H5Lget_info_by_idx. Returns H5L_info1_t metadata for the n-th link in a group according to the specified index and order.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier for the parent of group_name.
group_name may be '.' when loc_id is the group.
idx_type and order must be valid; n is zero-based.
linfo must be a valid pointer to H5L_info1_t.
lapl_id must be valid if not H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Literate1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Literate1(hid_t grp_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t *idx, H5L_iterate1_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Literate2. Iterates non-recursively over links in a group in a specified index/order using a callback of type H5L_iterate1_t. Supports resuming via idx.
requirements: grp_id must be a valid group identifier.
idx_type and order must be valid; links may be sorted as needed.
idx may be NULL or valid pointer for resume.
op must be a valid callback; op_data is passed through.
Behavior is undefined if group membership changes during iteration.

functions.name: H5Literate_by_name1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Literate_by_name1(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t *idx, H5L_iterate1_t op, void *op_data, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Literate_by_name2. Iterates non-recursively over links in the named group using a specified index and order and a callback of type H5L_iterate1_t. Supports resuming via idx.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid identifier; group_name identifies the group ('.' if loc_id is the group).
idx_type/order must be valid.
idx may be NULL or a valid pointer; op must be non-null callback; op_data passed through.
lapl_id must be valid if not H5P_DEFAULT.
Behavior is undefined if group membership changes during iteration.

functions.name: H5Lvisit1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lvisit1(hid_t grp_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5L_iterate1_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Lvisit2. Recursively visits all links starting from grp_id in the specified index and order using a callback of type H5L_iterate1_t.
requirements: grp_id must be a valid group identifier.
idx_type/order must be valid; creation-order request may fall back to name order where not tracked.
op must be a valid callback; op_data is passed through. Callback return values control traversal.

functions.name: H5Lvisit_by_name1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Lvisit_by_name1(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5L_iterate1_t op, void *op_data, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Deprecated in favor of H5Lvisit_by_name2. Recursively visits all links starting from the named group (loc_id/group_name) using the specified index and order and a callback of type H5L_iterate1_t.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location identifier; group_name identifies the start group ('.' if loc_id is the group).
idx_type and order must be valid enumerations; creation-order request may fall back to name order where not tracked.
op must be a valid callback; op_data is passed through.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list if used.

functions.name: H5Mcreate
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mcreate(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t key_type_id, hid_t val_type_id, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t mcpl_id, hid_t mapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a new HDF5 map object (key–value store) at the given location and link name, using the specified in-file key and value datatypes and property lists. Typical usage: create a map in a group or file, then use H5Mput/H5Mget/etc., and close the returned ID with H5Mclose when done.
requirements: loc_id must identify a valid location (file or group) where the map will be created.
name must be a valid non-NULL link name relative to loc_id.
key_type_id and val_type_id must be valid HDF5 datatype identifiers; these define the in-file datatypes for keys and values.
lcpl_id, mcpl_id, and mapl_id must be valid property list identifiers or H5P_DEFAULT as appropriate for link/map creation and access.
The returned map identifier must be closed with H5Mclose() when no longer needed.

functions.name: H5Mcreate_async
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mcreate_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t key_type_id, hid_t val_type_id, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t mcpl_id, hid_t mapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Mcreate. Schedules creation of a map object on the provided event set. In normal application code, call via the H5Mcreate_async(...) wrapper macro which supplies app_file/app_func/app_line automatically.
requirements: Typically invoked via the provided wrapper macro; if calling directly, app_file and app_func should be valid strings describing the call site and app_line the source line number.
loc_id must be a valid file or group location; name must be a valid non-NULL link name relative to loc_id.
key_type_id and val_type_id must be valid datatype identifiers.
lcpl_id, mcpl_id, mapl_id must be valid property lists or H5P_DEFAULT as appropriate.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier for async execution.
The returned map identifier must eventually be closed with H5Mclose().

functions.name: H5Mcreate_anon
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mcreate_anon(hid_t loc_id, hid_t key_type_id, hid_t val_type_id, hid_t mcpl_id, hid_t mapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a new map object that is not linked into the group hierarchy. The resulting ID can be linked later (e.g., with H5Olink) or it will be deleted when closed. Use this to create a map transiently or to link it later under multiple names.
requirements: loc_id must identify the target file in which to create the map (no link is created).
key_type_id and val_type_id must be valid datatype identifiers for the in-file key and value types.
mcpl_id and mapl_id must be valid property list IDs or H5P_DEFAULT as appropriate.
If the map is not linked into the file namespace before close, it will be deleted upon close.
The returned map identifier must be closed with H5Mclose() when no longer needed.

functions.name: H5Mopen
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mopen(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t mapl_id);
functions.description: Opens an existing map object by name relative to loc_id and returns a map identifier. Close with H5Mclose when done.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location (file or group) that contains the map link.
name must be a valid non-NULL link name to the map relative to loc_id.
mapl_id must be a valid map access property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
The returned map identifier must be closed with H5Mclose() when no longer needed.

functions.name: H5Mopen_async
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mopen_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t mapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Mopen. Schedules opening an existing map on the provided event set. In normal application code, call via the H5Mopen_async(...) wrapper macro which supplies app_file/app_func/app_line automatically.
requirements: Typically invoked via the provided wrapper macro; if calling directly, app_file and app_func should be valid strings and app_line a source line number.
loc_id must be a valid file or group location; name must be a valid non-NULL link name to the map.
mapl_id must be a valid map access property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.
The returned map identifier must be closed with H5Mclose().

functions.name: H5Mclose
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mclose(hid_t map_id);
functions.description: Closes a map object identifier and releases associated resources. After closing, the identifier must not be used.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier that is currently open.
After successful return, the same map_id must not be used in further map calls.

functions.name: H5Mclose_async
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mclose_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t map_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Mclose. Schedules closing a map identifier on the provided event set. Normally invoked through the H5Mclose_async(...) wrapper macro which supplies app_file/app_func/app_line.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.
Typically invoked via the wrapper macro; if calling directly, app_file and app_func should be valid strings and app_line a source line number.

functions.name: H5Mget_key_type
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mget_key_type(hid_t map_id);
functions.description: Returns an identifier for the in-file key datatype of the given map.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
The returned datatype identifier should be managed per HDF5 conventions (e.g., closed with H5Tclose) although this is not explicitly stated here.

functions.name: H5Mget_val_type
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mget_val_type(hid_t map_id);
functions.description: Returns an identifier for the in-file value datatype of the given map.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
The returned datatype identifier should be managed per HDF5 conventions (e.g., closed with H5Tclose), though not explicitly stated here.

functions.name: H5Mget_create_plist
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mget_create_plist(hid_t map_id);
functions.description: Returns an identifier for a copy of the creation property list (MCPL) used by the map.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
The returned property list identifier must be closed with H5Pclose() to prevent resource leaks.

functions.name: H5Mget_access_plist
functions.signature: hid_t H5Mget_access_plist(hid_t map_id);
functions.description: Returns an identifier for a copy of the map access property list (MAPL) for the map.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
The returned property list identifier should be closed with H5Pclose() per HDF5 conventions.

functions.name: H5Mget_count
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mget_count(hid_t map_id, hsize_t *count, hid_t dxpl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves the number of key–value pairs stored in the map.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
count must be a valid non-NULL pointer to storage for the result.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Mput
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mput(hid_t map_id, hid_t key_mem_type_id, const void *key, hid_t val_mem_type_id, const void *value, hid_t dxpl_id);
functions.description: Inserts or updates a key–value pair in the map. If the key exists, its value is updated; otherwise, a new pair is added. Key/value data are interpreted using the provided memory datatypes and converted to the map’s in-file types as needed.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
key_mem_type_id and val_mem_type_id must be valid datatype identifiers describing the memory layout of key and value.
key must point to a valid buffer matching key_mem_type_id; value must point to a valid buffer matching val_mem_type_id.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Mput_async
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mput_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t map_id, hid_t key_mem_type_id, const void *key, hid_t val_mem_type_id, const void *value, hid_t dxpl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Mput. Schedules insertion/update of a key–value pair on the provided event set. Normally invoked through the H5Mput_async(...) wrapper macro which supplies app_file/app_func/app_line.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
key_mem_type_id and val_mem_type_id must be valid datatype identifiers.
key and value must be valid non-NULL pointers to data matching the memory datatypes.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.
If calling directly (not via wrapper), app_file/app_func/app_line should describe the call site.

functions.name: H5Mget
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mget(hid_t map_id, hid_t key_mem_type_id, const void *key, hid_t val_mem_type_id, void *value, hid_t dxpl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves the value associated with the given key from the map, converting between memory and in-file datatypes as needed.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
key_mem_type_id and val_mem_type_id must be valid datatype identifiers.
key must point to a valid buffer describing the key in key_mem_type_id.
value must point to a valid, writable buffer suitable for the converted result as described by val_mem_type_id.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Mget_async
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mget_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t map_id, hid_t key_mem_type_id, const void *key, hid_t val_mem_type_id, void *value, hid_t dxpl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Mget. Schedules retrieval of a value by key on the provided event set. Normally invoked through the H5Mget_async(...) wrapper macro which supplies app_file/app_func/app_line.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
key_mem_type_id and val_mem_type_id must be valid datatype identifiers.
key must be a valid non-NULL pointer; value must be a valid writable buffer.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
es_id must be a valid event set identifier.
If calling directly (not via wrapper), app_file/app_func/app_line should describe the call site.

functions.name: H5Mexists
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mexists(hid_t map_id, hid_t key_mem_type_id, const void *key, bool *exists, hid_t dxpl_id);
functions.description: Checks whether the given key exists in the map. If the memory datatype differs from the map’s in-file key datatype, the key is converted internally for the query.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
key_mem_type_id must be a valid datatype identifier for the key buffer.
key must point to a valid buffer describing the key.
exists must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a bool to receive the result.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Miterate
functions.signature: herr_t H5Miterate(hid_t map_id, hsize_t *idx, hid_t key_mem_type_id, H5M_iterate_t op, void *op_data, hid_t dxpl_id);
functions.description: Iterates over all key–value pairs in the map, invoking the user callback for each. The idx parameter is in/out: set idx=0 to start; reuse the returned idx to resume a later iteration. The callback receives the map ID, the current key (converted to key_mem_type_id), and op_data. A negative callback return signals error; a positive return stops iteration without error; zero continues.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
idx must be a valid non-NULL pointer; set *idx to 0 to start iteration or to the prior returned value to resume.
key_mem_type_id must be a valid datatype identifier for the desired key memory type.
op must be a valid non-NULL function pointer of type H5M_iterate_t; op_data may be NULL or a valid user context pointer.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
Do not add or remove key–value pairs in the map during iteration; doing so leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: H5Miterate_by_name
functions.signature: herr_t H5Miterate_by_name(hid_t loc_id, const char *map_name, hsize_t *idx, hid_t key_mem_type_id, H5M_iterate_t op, void *op_data, hid_t dxpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Iterates over all key–value pairs in the named map located under loc_id, invoking the user callback for each. Semantics and callback behavior are the same as H5Miterate, with link traversal controlled by lapl_id.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group location that can resolve map_name.
map_name must be a valid non-NULL name of the map relative to loc_id.
idx must be a valid non-NULL pointer; set *idx to 0 to start or to a prior value to resume.
key_mem_type_id must be a valid datatype identifier for the desired key memory type.
op must be a valid non-NULL function pointer of type H5M_iterate_t; op_data may be NULL.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
Do not add or remove key–value pairs in the map during iteration; doing so leads to undefined behavior.

functions.name: H5Mdelete
functions.signature: herr_t H5Mdelete(hid_t map_id, hid_t key_mem_type_id, const void *key, hid_t dxpl_id);
functions.description: Deletes the key–value pair identified by the given key from the map. If the provided key memory datatype differs from the map’s in-file key datatype, the key is converted internally for the lookup.
requirements: map_id must be a valid map object identifier.
key_mem_type_id must be a valid datatype identifier.
key must point to a valid buffer describing the key.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.

functions.name: H5Oopen
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Oopen(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Opens an HDF5 object (group, dataset, or committed datatype) by path relative to loc_id without needing to know its type. Use when you have a path and want a generic object handle; determine type via H5Iget_type(). Close the returned id with H5Oclose/H5Gclose/H5Dclose/H5Tclose.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file, group, dataset, named datatype, or attribute identifier; if an attribute id is supplied, the attached object is used
name must be a valid path to an existing object relative to loc_id (or absolute)
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT
Caller must close the returned object id when done to avoid leaks

functions.name: H5Oopen_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Oopen_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Oopen. Schedules opening an object by path and returns immediately; completion is tracked via an event set es_id. app_file/app_func/app_line are auto-filled by wrapper macros for diagnostics.
requirements: loc_id, name, lapl_id requirements are the same as H5Oopen
es_id must be a valid event set identifier for async operations
Do not assume the object is ready until the event is complete; follow the VOL/async completion model
Close the returned object id after use

functions.name: H5Oopen_by_token
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Oopen_by_token(hid_t loc_id, H5O_token_t token);
functions.description: Opens an object by a VOL connector object token within the context of loc_id. Use when you have a persistent token rather than a path.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group identifier within the same VOL connector class as the token
token must be a valid object token originating from the same connector/file scope
Caller must close the returned object id

functions.name: H5Oopen_by_idx
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Oopen_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Opens the nth object in a group according to a specified index and order. Useful for indexed traversal without separate iteration.
requirements: loc_id must identify a location in the file; if it already identifies the target group, group_name can be "."
group_name must name a group relative to loc_id (or ".")
idx_type must be a valid H5_index_t; group may be sorted/indexed as needed
order must be a valid H5_iter_order_t
n is zero-based index into the chosen ordering and must be within range
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT
Caller must close the returned object id

functions.name: H5Oopen_by_idx_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Oopen_by_idx_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Oopen_by_idx. Schedules opening the nth object in a group according to index/order; completion tracked via es_id.
requirements: Same argument requirements as H5Oopen_by_idx for loc_id, group_name, idx_type, order, n, lapl_id
es_id must be a valid async event set
Do not use the returned id until the operation completes per async API
Caller must close the object id

functions.name: H5Oexists_by_name
functions.signature: H5_DLL htri_t H5Oexists_by_name(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Checks whether the link at name (relative to loc_id) resolves to an existing object (not dangling). Returns >0 if exists, 0 if not, <0 on error. Useful to validate targets of soft/external links.
requirements: loc_id must identify a valid location (file/group/etc.); if an attribute id is supplied, the attached object is used
name must be a link path; intermediate path elements must exist or the call fails
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT
Caller must handle tri-state return: positive -> exists, 0 -> does not resolve, negative -> error

functions.name: H5Oget_info3
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info3(hid_t loc_id, H5O_info2_t *oinfo, unsigned fields);
functions.description: Retrieves selected metadata (per fields mask) about the object identified by loc_id into H5O_info2_t. Use to query type, refcount, times, num_attrs, token, etc.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid object identifier
oinfo must be a non-NULL pointer to writable H5O_info2_t
fields must be a combination of H5O_INFO_BASIC, H5O_INFO_TIME, H5O_INFO_NUM_ATTRS

functions.name: H5Oget_info_by_name3
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info_by_name3(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5O_info2_t *oinfo, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves selected metadata about an object specified by name relative to loc_id into H5O_info2_t, controlled by fields mask.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location id
name must reference an existing object (relative, absolute, or ".")
oinfo must be a non-NULL writable pointer
fields is a combination of H5O_INFO_* flags
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT

functions.name: H5Oget_info_by_name_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info_by_name_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5O_info2_t *oinfo, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Oget_info_by_name3. Schedules retrieval of object info by name; results filled into oinfo upon completion.
requirements: Same as H5Oget_info_by_name3 for loc_id, name, oinfo, fields, lapl_id
es_id must be a valid event set
Caller must ensure oinfo remains valid until operation completion

functions.name: H5Oget_info_by_idx3
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info_by_idx3(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5O_info2_t *oinfo, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves selected metadata about the nth object in a group according to an index and order, writing into H5O_info2_t.
requirements: loc_id valid; group_name names a group relative to loc_id (or ".")
idx_type and order must be valid enumeration values
n is zero-based position and must be within bounds
oinfo must be non-NULL and writable
fields is combination of H5O_INFO_* flags
lapl_id must be H5P_DEFAULT or a valid link access property list

functions.name: H5Oget_native_info
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_native_info(hid_t loc_id, H5O_native_info_t *oinfo, unsigned fields);
functions.description: Returns native file format object header and metadata size information for the object identified by loc_id into H5O_native_info_t, controlled by fields mask H5O_NATIVE_INFO_*.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid object identifier
oinfo must be non-NULL and writable
fields must be a combination of H5O_NATIVE_INFO_HDR and/or H5O_NATIVE_INFO_META_SIZE

functions.name: H5Oget_native_info_by_name
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_native_info_by_name(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5O_native_info_t *oinfo, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Returns native file format information for an object specified by name relative to loc_id into H5O_native_info_t, per fields mask.
requirements: loc_id valid; name must resolve to an object (relative, absolute, or ".")
oinfo must be non-NULL and writable
fields is a combination of H5O_NATIVE_INFO_* flags
lapl_id must be H5P_DEFAULT or a valid link access property list

functions.name: H5Oget_native_info_by_idx
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_native_info_by_idx(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5O_native_info_t *oinfo, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Returns native file format information for the nth object in a group by index/order into H5O_native_info_t.
requirements: loc_id valid; group_name names a group relative to loc_id (or ".")
idx_type and order must be valid
n zero-based index must be in range
oinfo must be non-NULL and writable
fields is combination of H5O_NATIVE_INFO_* flags
lapl_id must be H5P_DEFAULT or a valid link access property list

functions.name: H5Olink
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Olink(hid_t obj_id, hid_t new_loc_id, const char *new_name, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Creates a new hard link (additional name) to an existing object obj_id at new_loc_id/new_name. Commonly used to link anonymously-created objects or share objects across groups.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid group, dataset, or committed datatype to link
new_loc_id must be a valid location (file/group/dataset/named datatype/attribute id); if attribute id, the attached object is used
new_name must be a valid link name path relative to new_loc_id and must not already exist
lcpl_id and lapl_id must be valid property list ids or H5P_DEFAULT; enable intermediate group creation with appropriate LCPL setting if needed

functions.name: H5Oincr_refcount
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oincr_refcount(hid_t object_id);
functions.description: Manually increments an object's hard link reference count. Intended when adding user-defined links that reference objects by address.
requirements: object_id must be a valid object (dataset, group, or committed datatype)
Use with care; ensure corresponding decrement via H5Odecr_refcount when link is deleted to avoid leaks or corruption

functions.name: H5Odecr_refcount
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Odecr_refcount(hid_t object_id);
functions.description: Manually decrements an object's hard link reference count. Intended when removing user-defined links that reference objects by address.
requirements: object_id must be a valid object (dataset, group, or committed datatype)
Use with care; incorrect use can lead to inaccessible data or corruption

functions.name: H5Ocopy
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ocopy(hid_t src_loc_id, const char *src_name, hid_t dst_loc_id, const char *dst_name, hid_t ocpypl_id, hid_t lcpl_id);
functions.description: Copies a group, dataset, or committed datatype from src_loc_id/src_name to dst_loc_id/dst_name. Behavior controlled by object copy and link creation property lists (flags for expanding links, copying attributes, merging committed dtypes, etc.).
requirements: src_loc_id must identify a valid location; src_name must identify an existing source object (path can traverse soft/external per options)
dst_loc_id must be a valid destination location; if a file id, root group is used
dst_name must not already exist at destination; absolute paths are relative to root
ocpypl_id and lcpl_id must be valid property lists or H5P_DEFAULT; set LCPL to create intermediate groups if needed
If the source object was modified, ensure it’s flushed/closed before copying to avoid stale state

functions.name: H5Ocopy_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ocopy_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t src_loc_id, const char *src_name, hid_t dst_loc_id, const char *dst_name, hid_t ocpypl_id, hid_t lcpl_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Ocopy. Schedules an object copy operation; completion tracked via es_id.
requirements: Same as H5Ocopy for src/dst ids, names, ocpypl_id, lcpl_id
es_id must be a valid event set
Do not use the destination object until operation completion per async semantics

functions.name: H5Oset_comment
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oset_comment(hid_t obj_id, const char *comment);
functions.description: Sets or removes the comment on the specified object. Passing NULL or empty string removes any existing comment. Comments are short, null-terminated ASCII strings.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid object identifier (datasets, groups, committed datatypes)
comment may be NULL/"" to remove; otherwise should be a null-terminated ASCII string

functions.name: H5Oset_comment_by_name
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oset_comment_by_name(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, const char *comment, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Sets or removes the comment on the object addressed by name relative to loc_id. lapl_id controls link traversal. NULL or empty comment removes it.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location id; name must resolve to the target object (relative, absolute, or ".")
comment may be NULL/"" to remove; otherwise should be a null-terminated ASCII string
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT

functions.name: H5Oget_comment
functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Oget_comment(hid_t obj_id, char *comment, size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Retrieves the comment for the specified object into comment buffer. Returns the comment length (excluding null), or 0 if none. You can query required size by passing comment=NULL.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid object identifier
If comment is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least bufsize bytes; function may return a value larger than bufsize indicating truncation
When comment is NULL, bufsize is ignored and the return value is the required size without the null terminator

functions.name: H5Oget_comment_by_name
functions.signature: H5_DLL ssize_t H5Oget_comment_by_name(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, char *comment, size_t bufsize, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Retrieves the comment for the object addressed by name relative to loc_id. Returns length (excluding null), or 0 if none. Passing comment=NULL queries required size.
requirements: loc_id must be valid; name must resolve to an object (relative, absolute, or ".")
If comment is non-NULL, buffer must be at least bufsize bytes
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT

functions.name: H5Ovisit3
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ovisit3(hid_t obj_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5O_iterate2_t op, void *op_data, unsigned fields);
functions.description: Recursively visits obj_id and, if it’s a group or file (root), all reachable objects, invoking callback op for each. The fields mask controls which H5O_info2_t fields are populated for the callback.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid id; for file id, iteration starts at root; for attribute id, iterates attached object; for non-group/dataset/type, no recursive traversal
idx_type and order select iteration index and traversal order; creation-order traversal may fall back to name order if not tracked
op must be a valid function pointer; its return conventions control iteration; op_data is passed through
fields must be a combination of H5O_INFO_* flags
Group membership must remain unchanged during iteration; behavior is undefined otherwise

functions.name: H5Ovisit_by_name3
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ovisit_by_name3(hid_t loc_id, const char *obj_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5O_iterate2_t op, void *op_data, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: Recursively visits the object addressed by obj_name relative to loc_id and all reachable objects (if group), invoking op. fields controls info populated for callback; lapl_id affects link traversal (e.g., external link prefixes).
requirements: loc_id must be valid; obj_name must identify the root object (absolute, relative, or ".")
idx_type and order must be valid; creation-order traversal may fall back to name order if not tracked
op must be a valid callback; op_data is passed through
fields is combination of H5O_INFO_* flags
lapl_id must be a valid link access property list or H5P_DEFAULT
Group membership must remain unchanged during iteration

functions.name: H5Oclose
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oclose(hid_t object_id);
functions.description: Closes an HDF5 object (group, dataset, or named datatype) previously opened. Equivalent to the type-specific close calls.
requirements: object_id must be a valid open object id for a group, dataset, or named datatype
Must be called once per open to release resources; do not use object_id after closing

functions.name: H5Oclose_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oclose_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t object_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Oclose. Schedules closing of object_id; completion tracked via es_id.
requirements: object_id must be a valid open object id
es_id must be a valid async event set
Do not use object_id after the close operation completes; follow async semantics

functions.name: H5Oflush
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oflush(hid_t obj_id);
functions.description: Flushes HDF5 and OS buffers associated with the named object to storage without evicting from cache. Not reliable with parallel I/O (known issue).
requirements: obj_id must be a valid named object id (dataset, group, committed datatype)
Be aware: in parallel usage it may cause assertion failure during H5Fclose per warning

functions.name: H5Oflush_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oflush_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t obj_id, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Oflush. Schedules a flush of the object’s buffers; completion via es_id.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid named object id
es_id must be a valid async event set
Parallel limitations from H5Oflush apply

functions.name: H5Orefresh
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Orefresh(hid_t oid);
functions.description: Refreshes an object: clears cached metadata and reloads from disk, re-registering under the same identifier. Use to see external changes in SWMR-like workflows.
requirements: oid must be a valid named object id (dataset, group, committed datatype)

functions.name: H5Orefresh_async
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Orefresh_async(const char *app_file, const char *app_func, unsigned app_line, hid_t oid, hid_t es_id);
functions.description: Asynchronous variant of H5Orefresh. Schedules refresh of the object; completion tracked via es_id.
requirements: oid must be a valid named object id
es_id must be a valid async event set

functions.name: H5Odisable_mdc_flushes
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Odisable_mdc_flushes(hid_t object_id);
functions.description: Prevents flushing of dirty metadata cache entries for the specified object by the normal cache policy; requires manual flushing via H5*flush calls.
requirements: object_id must be a dataset, group, or committed datatype identifier (not a file id or other kind)
Calling on an object that already has flushes disabled returns an error
Caller must manage memory pressure; misuse can exhaust cache memory

functions.name: H5Oenable_mdc_flushes
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oenable_mdc_flushes(hid_t object_id);
functions.description: Re-enables normal eviction/flush of dirty metadata cache entries for the specified object.
requirements: object_id must be a dataset, group, or committed datatype identifier (not a file id)
Calling on an object that has not had flushes disabled is an error
State can be queried with H5Oare_mdc_flushes_disabled
Objects revert to default behavior on close; all revert on file close

functions.name: H5Oare_mdc_flushes_disabled
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oare_mdc_flushes_disabled(hid_t object_id, bool *are_disabled);
functions.description: Reports whether metadata cache flushes have been disabled for the specified object via H5Odisable_mdc_flushes.
requirements: object_id must be a dataset, group, or committed datatype identifier (not a file id)
are_disabled must be a non-NULL pointer to bool storage

functions.name: H5Otoken_cmp
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Otoken_cmp(hid_t loc_id, const H5O_token_t *token1, const H5O_token_t *token2, int *cmp_value);
functions.description: Compares two VOL object tokens from the same connector/file context and returns ordering in cmp_value (>0, <0, or 0).
requirements: loc_id must be a file or group id appropriate for the tokens’ connector class
token1 and token2 must be non-NULL pointers to tokens from the same VOL class/context
cmp_value must be a non-NULL pointer to int for result

functions.name: H5Otoken_to_str
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Otoken_to_str(hid_t loc_id, const H5O_token_t *token, char **token_str);
functions.description: Serializes a connector’s object token into a newly-allocated string representation. Use for persistence or debugging.
requirements: loc_id must match the token’s VOL class/context
token must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid token

token_str must be a non-NULL pointer; on success, *token_str will point to an allocated string which the caller must eventually free via the library’s documented deallocator (unknown from this header)

functions.name: H5Otoken_from_str
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Otoken_from_str(hid_t loc_id, const char *token_str, H5O_token_t *token);
functions.description: Deserializes a string form of an object token into an H5O_token_t for the given connector/file context.
requirements: loc_id must match the intended token’s VOL class/context
token_str must be a non-NULL, valid serialization produced by H5Otoken_to_str for the same connector context
token must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage

functions.name: H5Oopen_by_addr
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Oopen_by_addr(hid_t loc_id, haddr_t addr);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Opens an object by its on-disk address (object header offset). Superseded by H5Oopen_by_token. Dangerous if address is invalid.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid location id within the file containing the object
addr must be a valid object header address retrieved immediately before use (e.g., via H5Lget_info/H5Gget_objinfo) to avoid reuse issues
Caller must close the returned id; misuse can corrupt files

functions.name: H5Oget_info1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info1(hid_t loc_id, H5O_info1_t *oinfo);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Retrieves full object info (legacy H5O_info1_t) for the object identified by loc_id.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid object id
oinfo must be a non-NULL pointer to writable H5O_info1_t

functions.name: H5Oget_info_by_name1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info_by_name1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5O_info1_t *oinfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Retrieves legacy H5O_info1_t for an object addressed by name relative to loc_id.
requirements: loc_id valid; name must resolve to an object (relative, absolute, or ".")
oinfo must be non-NULL and writable
lapl_id must be H5P_DEFAULT or valid link access property list

functions.name: H5Oget_info_by_idx1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info_by_idx1(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5O_info1_t *oinfo, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Retrieves legacy H5O_info1_t for the nth object in a group by index and order.
requirements: loc_id valid; group_name names a group relative to loc_id (or ".")
idx_type and order valid; n is zero-based within range
oinfo must be non-NULL and writable
lapl_id must be H5P_DEFAULT or valid link access property list

functions.name: H5Oget_info2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info2(hid_t loc_id, H5O_info1_t *oinfo, unsigned fields);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Retrieves selected legacy info fields into H5O_info1_t for object identified by loc_id, as controlled by fields mask.
requirements: loc_id must be valid
oinfo must be non-NULL and writable
fields must be a combination of H5O_INFO_* flags (legacy set)

functions.name: H5Oget_info_by_name2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info_by_name2(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, H5O_info1_t *oinfo, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Retrieves selected legacy fields into H5O_info1_t for an object addressed by name, controlled by fields mask.
requirements: loc_id valid; name resolves to an object
oinfo non-NULL and writable
fields is combination of H5O_INFO_* flags
lapl_id must be H5P_DEFAULT or valid link access property list

functions.name: H5Oget_info_by_idx2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Oget_info_by_idx2(hid_t loc_id, const char *group_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, hsize_t n, H5O_info1_t *oinfo, unsigned fields, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Retrieves selected legacy info for the nth object in a group by index/order into H5O_info1_t.
requirements: loc_id valid; group_name names a group (or ".")
idx_type/order valid; n within range
oinfo non-NULL and writable
fields combination of H5O_INFO_* flags
lapl_id H5P_DEFAULT or valid link access property list

functions.name: H5Ovisit1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ovisit1(hid_t obj_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5O_iterate1_t op, void *op_data);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Recursively visits objects starting from obj_id, invoking legacy callback with H5O_info1_t.
requirements: obj_id must be valid; traversal semantics like H5Ovisit3
idx_type/order valid
op must be a valid callback; op_data passed through
Group membership must remain unchanged during iteration

functions.name: H5Ovisit_by_name1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ovisit_by_name1(hid_t loc_id, const char *obj_name, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5O_iterate1_t op, void *op_data, hid_t lapl_id);
functions.description: [Deprecated] Recursively visits the object addressed by obj_name relative to loc_id using legacy callback (H5O_info1_t).
requirements: loc_id valid; obj_name identifies root object
idx_type/order valid
op callback valid; op_data passed through
lapl_id must be H5P_DEFAULT or valid link access property list
Group membership must remain unchanged during iteration

functions.name: H5Ovisit2
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Ovisit2(hid_t obj_id, H5_index_t idx_type, H5_iter_order_t order, H5O_iterate1_t op, void *op_data, unsigned fields);
