functions.description: Reclaims memory buffers allocated for variable-length (VL) datatype data within the selection of space_id. Uses plist_id to determine custom alloc/free methods used during I/O.
requirements: type_id must be a valid datatype id corresponding to the VL data layout in buf.
space_id must be a valid dataspace id describing the selection to reclaim.
plist_id must be the dataset transfer property list used to create the buffers.
buf must point to the data buffer containing VL elements to reclaim.

functions.name: H5Tdecode1
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Tdecode1(const void *buf);
functions.description: Deprecated: Old name for H5Tdecode(). Decodes a binary-encoded datatype description and returns a new datatype id. Prefer H5Tdecode2() or macro H5Tdecode. Caller must close with H5Tclose().
requirements: buf must point to a valid encoded datatype buffer produced by H5Tencode().
Returned datatype id must be closed with H5Tclose().

functions.name: H5Tcommit1
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Tcommit1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name, hid_t type_id);
functions.description: Deprecated: Old name for H5Tcommit(). Commits a transient datatype to a file with the given name using default properties. Fails for empty compound/enum types.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group id.
name must be a valid path to create the committed datatype (intermediate groups must exist).
type_id must be a transient datatype that can hold data (not empty compound/enum).

functions.name: H5Topen1
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Topen1(hid_t loc_id, const char *name);
functions.description: Deprecated: Old name for H5Topen(). Opens a named committed datatype. Caller must close with H5Tclose().
requirements: loc_id must be a valid file or group id.
name must identify an existing committed datatype.
Returned datatype id must be closed with H5Tclose().

functions.name: H5Tarray_create1
functions.signature: H5_DLL hid_t H5Tarray_create1(hid_t base_id, int ndims, const hsize_t dim[], const int perm[]);
functions.description: Deprecated: Old name for H5Tarray_create(). Creates an array datatype of rank ndims with sizes dim; perm parameter for permutations is not implemented/unused. Returns datatype id to be closed with H5Tclose().
requirements: base_id must be a valid datatype id.
ndims must be > 0 and <= H5S_MAX_RANK.
Each dim[i] must be > 0.
perm is currently unused.
Returned datatype id must be closed with H5Tclose().

functions.name: H5Tget_array_dims1
functions.signature: H5_DLL int H5Tget_array_dims1(hid_t type_id, hsize_t dims[], int perm[]);
functions.description: Deprecated: Old name for H5Tget_array_dims(). Returns sizes of array dimensions into dims and (unused) perm. Returns the number of dimensions.
requirements: type_id must be a valid array datatype id.
dims must be a buffer large enough for all dimensions.
perm parameter is not used.

functions.name: H5VLregister_connector_by_name
functions.signature: hid_t H5VLregister_connector_by_name(const char *connector_name, hid_t vipl_id);
functions.description: Registers a new VOL connector with the HDF5 library by its name and returns a VOL connector identifier. Typical usage is to enable a VOL connector by name; the returned ID can later be closed with H5VLclose() or unregistered with H5VLunregister_connector() as appropriate.
requirements: connector_name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the VOL connector.
vipl_id must be either H5P_DEFAULT or a valid property list ID of class H5P_VOL_INITIALIZE created with H5Pcreate().
On success, the returned VOL connector identifier should be released with H5VLclose() when no longer needed.
Do not assume registration succeeds for an unknown name; callers must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5VLregister_connector_by_value
functions.signature: hid_t H5VLregister_connector_by_value(H5VL_class_value_t connector_value, hid_t vipl_id);
functions.description: Registers a new VOL connector with the HDF5 library by its numeric class value and returns a VOL connector identifier. Use when the connector’s numeric value is known; the returned ID can be closed with H5VLclose() or unregistered with H5VLunregister_connector().
requirements: connector_value must be a valid H5VL_class_value_t for the target connector. Values 0–255 are library-defined; 256–511 are for testing; subsequent values are assigned by The HDF Group.
vipl_id must be either H5P_DEFAULT or a valid property list ID of class H5P_VOL_INITIALIZE created with H5Pcreate().
On success, the returned VOL connector identifier should be released with H5VLclose() when no longer needed.
Callers must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5VLis_connector_registered_by_name
functions.signature: htri_t H5VLis_connector_registered_by_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Checks whether a VOL connector has been registered under the given name. Returns a tri-state value: positive for true, 0 for false, and negative for error.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
Callers must interpret negative return values as errors and not as boolean false.

functions.name: H5VLis_connector_registered_by_value
functions.signature: htri_t H5VLis_connector_registered_by_value(H5VL_class_value_t connector_value);
functions.description: Checks whether a VOL connector has been registered for the given numeric class value. Returns positive for true, 0 for false, negative for error.
requirements: connector_value should be within the defined ranges for H5VL_class_value_t (0–255 library-defined; 256–511 testing; higher by assignment).
Callers must interpret negative return values as errors and not as boolean false.

functions.name: H5VLget_connector_id
functions.signature: hid_t H5VLget_connector_id(hid_t obj_id);
functions.description: Retrieves the registered VOL connector identifier associated with the specified HDF5 object identifier. The returned VOL connector ID must be closed with H5VLclose() when no longer needed.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid HDF5 object identifier (e.g., file, group, dataset, etc.).
On success, the returned VOL connector identifier must be closed with H5VLclose() to avoid resource leaks.
Callers must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5VLget_connector_id_by_name
functions.signature: hid_t H5VLget_connector_id_by_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Obtains the VOL connector identifier for a registered connector with the given name. The returned ID should be closed with H5VLclose() when no longer in use.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string corresponding to a registered connector name.
On success, the returned VOL connector identifier must be closed with H5VLclose().
Callers must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5VLget_connector_id_by_value
functions.signature: hid_t H5VLget_connector_id_by_value(H5VL_class_value_t connector_value);
functions.description: Obtains the VOL connector identifier for a registered connector with the given numeric class value. The returned ID should be closed with H5VLclose() when no longer in use.
requirements: connector_value must correspond to a registered VOL connector (value ranges: 0–255 library-defined; 256–511 testing; higher by assignment).
On success, the returned VOL connector identifier must be closed with H5VLclose().
Callers must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5VLget_connector_name
functions.signature: ssize_t H5VLget_connector_name(hid_t id, char *name, size_t size);
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the VOL connector associated with the given object or file identifier. Returns the length of the connector name on success. If querying the required size, pass a NULL name pointer; note the header documentation ambiguously mentions “NULL pointer for size,” but the typical HDF5 pattern is name==NULL to query length.
requirements: id must be a valid object or file identifier associated with a VOL connector.
If name is non-NULL, size specifies the maximum number of characters to write; the buffer must be at least size bytes.
To query the required buffer size without writing a name, pass name==NULL (as commonly used in HDF5 APIs; the comment’s reference to NULL size appears to be a documentation typo).
Callers must check for a negative return value indicating failure.

functions.name: H5VLclose
functions.signature: herr_t H5VLclose(hid_t connector_id);
functions.description: Closes a VOL connector identifier, releasing the library reference to the connector. Does not affect file access property lists or open files that use the connector.
requirements: connector_id must be a valid VOL connector identifier previously obtained (e.g., from registration or lookup).
After successful close, the connector_id must not be used again.
Callers must check the return status; a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5VLunregister_connector
functions.signature: herr_t H5VLunregister_connector(hid_t connector_id);
functions.description: Unregisters a VOL connector from the library. This does not affect file access property lists or any files already opened with this connector. Attempting to unregister the native VOL connector will fail.
requirements: connector_id must refer to a registered VOL connector.
It is an error to attempt to unregister the native VOL connector.
Callers must check the return status; a negative value indicates failure.
Unregistering does not close existing identifiers; separate H5VLclose() calls may still be required for outstanding IDs.

functions.name: H5VLquery_optional
functions.signature: herr_t H5VLquery_optional(hid_t obj_id, H5VL_subclass_t subcls, int opt_type, uint64_t *flags);
functions.description: Determines whether a VOL connector associated with an object supports a particular optional operation and returns capability flags describing the operation’s properties (e.g., read/write metadata/data, collective, async).
requirements: obj_id must be a valid HDF5 object identifier whose associated VOL is being queried.
subcls must be a valid H5VL_subclass_t indicating the targeted VOL subclass.
opt_type must identify the optional operation code meaningful to the VOL connector.
flags must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a bitmask of H5VL_OPT_QUERY_* flags.
Callers must check the return status; a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5VLobject_is_native
functions.signature: herr_t H5VLobject_is_native(hid_t obj_id, bool *is_native);
functions.description: Reports whether the given object identifier is associated with the native VOL connector. Writes a boolean result to is_native.
requirements: obj_id must be a valid HDF5 object identifier.
is_native must be a non-NULL pointer to a bool for the result.
Callers must check the return status; a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5Zfilter_avail
functions.signature: H5_DLL htri_t H5Zfilter_avail(H5Z_filter_t id);
functions.description: Determines whether the specified HDF5 filter is available in the current process. Typical usage is to pass a predefined H5Z_FILTER_* constant (e.g., H5Z_FILTER_DEFLATE) and then interpret the tri-state return value to decide whether the filter can be used to encode/decode datasets. Call this before configuring property lists that require a specific filter.
requirements: id must be a valid filter identifier (H5Z_filter_t), typically one of the H5Z_FILTER_* values or a registered filter id.
Caller must interpret the tri-state return: >0 means available, 0 means not available, <0 indicates an error and the result is invalid.
No output parameters are provided; there are no additional preconditions stated. Thread-safety or initialization requirements are unknown.

functions.name: H5Zget_filter_info
functions.signature: H5_DLL herr_t H5Zget_filter_info(H5Z_filter_t filter, unsigned int *filter_config_flags);
functions.description: Retrieves configuration information for a filter, indicating whether encoding and/or decoding is enabled. On success, if filter_config_flags is non-NULL, it is set to a bitfield composed of H5Z_FILTER_CONFIG_ENCODE_ENABLED and/or H5Z_FILTER_CONFIG_DECODE_ENABLED. Call this to verify that a filter supports the needed direction (encode for writing, decode for reading) before configuring datasets or reading files that use the filter.
requirements: filter must be a valid filter identifier (H5Z_filter_t) recognized by the library; passing an unknown filter id may cause the function to fail (negative return).
filter_config_flags may be NULL. If non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for an unsigned int to receive the bitfield result.
On success, the caller should test bits via (flags & H5Z_FILTER_CONFIG_ENCODE_ENABLED) and/or (flags & H5Z_FILTER_CONFIG_DECODE_ENABLED).
Caller must check the return value: non-negative indicates success; negative indicates failure and any output is invalid.

functions.name: H5DOappend
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DOappend(hid_t dset_id, hid_t dxpl_id, unsigned axis, size_t extension, hid_t memtype, const void *buf);
functions.description: Appends data to a dataset along a single (0-based) dimension. Internally extends the dataset by `extension` elements along `axis`, selects the appended hyperslab, and writes `buf` data using `memtype` via the transfer property list `dxpl_id`. Use when you need to grow a dataset along one dimension and immediately populate the new region without manually calling H5Dset_extent, H5Sselect_hyperslab, and H5Dwrite. Returns non-negative on success and negative on failure (typical HDF5 herr_t behavior). Notes: the target dimension must be extendible; for multi-dimensional datasets, the appended region is a contiguous hyperslab across the other dimensions.
requirements: dset_id must be a valid HDF5 dataset identifier.
axis must be 0-based and less than the dataset’s rank.
The dataset must be extendible along the specified axis (its maximum size must allow extension; typically requires chunked layout).
extension should be greater than 0 to append any data; if zero, no data would be appended (behavior not explicitly documented).
buf must point to at least extension * (product of sizes of all other dimensions) elements in memory, described by memtype.
memtype must be a valid HDF5 datatype identifier compatible with the dataset’s datatype.
dxpl_id must be a valid dataset transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
Caller should check the return value: a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5DOwrite_chunk
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DOwrite_chunk(hid_t dset_id, hid_t dxpl_id, uint32_t filters, const hsize_t *offset, size_t data_size, const void *buf);
functions.description: DEPRECATED in favor of H5Dwrite_chunk (since 1.10.3). Writes a raw data chunk directly to a chunked dataset, bypassing the normal HDF5 I/O pipeline (hyperslab selection, datatype conversion, and filters). `offset` specifies the logical position of the chunk; `buf` contains the raw (often preprocessed/compressed) chunk bytes of length `data_size`; `filters` is a bitmask indicating which filters in the pipeline were skipped (bit set means skipped). Use to write preprocessed chunk data directly for performance; in newer code, call H5Dwrite_chunk instead. Returns non-negative on success and negative on failure.
requirements: dset_id must be a valid HDF5 dataset identifier referring to a chunked dataset.
Not supported under parallel HDF5.
Variable-length datatypes are not supported.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
offset must be an array of length equal to the dataset rank; values must be within dataspace limits and must locate exactly on a chunk boundary.

filters is a 32-bit mask where a set bit at position p (0 ≤ p < 32) indicates the corresponding filter in the pipeline was skipped; zero means all enabled filters applied. The mask is stored with the chunk.
data_size must be the exact number of bytes to write from buf; for precompressed chunks, this is the compressed size.
buf must be non-null and point to at least data_size bytes of data to write.
Caller should check the return value: a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5DOread_chunk
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DOread_chunk(hid_t dset_id, hid_t dxpl_id, const hsize_t *offset, uint32_t *filters /*out*/, void *buf /*out*/);
functions.description: DEPRECATED in favor of H5Dread_chunk (since 1.10.3). Reads a raw data chunk directly from a chunked dataset at the given logical chunk `offset` into `buf`, bypassing the normal HDF5 I/O pipeline (including filters). On return, `*filters` indicates which filters were skipped when the chunk was written (bit set means skipped). Use for direct access to raw chunk bytes; in newer code, call H5Dread_chunk instead. Returns non-negative on success and negative on failure.
requirements: dset_id must be a valid HDF5 dataset identifier referring to a chunked dataset.
Not supported under parallel HDF5.
Variable-length datatypes are not supported.
dxpl_id must be a valid data transfer property list identifier or H5P_DEFAULT.
offset must be an array of length equal to the dataset rank; values must be within dataspace limits and must locate exactly on a chunk boundary.

filters must be a valid non-null pointer to a uint32_t to receive the filter mask; on return, a set bit at position p (0 ≤ p < 32) indicates the corresponding filter in the pipeline was skipped; zero means all enabled filters applied.
buf must be a valid non-null pointer to sufficient memory to receive one raw chunk’s bytes (size equals the on-disk chunk byte size, which may be compressed).
Caller should check the return value: a negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: H5DSwith_new_ref
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DSwith_new_ref(hid_t obj_id, bool *with_new_ref);
functions.description: Determines whether “new references” are used for dimension scales in the context of the provided object identifier. Typical usage: pass any valid HDF5 object ID and receive a boolean indicating if new references are in effect (e.g., when using a non-native VOL connector or when configured via H5_DIMENSION_SCALES_WITH_NEW_REF).
requirements: obj_id must be a valid HDF5 object identifier.
with_new_ref must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for a bool.
Caller must check the herr_t return value for errors before using the output flag.

functions.name: H5DSattach_scale
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DSattach_scale(hid_t did, hid_t dsid, unsigned int idx);
functions.description: Attaches a dimension scale dataset (dsid) to the specified dimension (idx) of a dataset (did). This updates the DIMENSION_LIST attribute on did and the REFERENCE_LIST attribute on the scale. Attaching the same scale more than once to the same dimension has no effect.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier that is not itself a Dimension Scale.
dsid must be a valid dataset identifier that is a Dimension Scale (i.e., previously converted via H5DSset_scale).
idx must refer to a valid dimension index of did (0-based, less than the dataset’s rank).
The datasets involved must exist; bad arguments cause failure.
Caller must check the herr_t return value for success/failure.

functions.name: H5DSdetach_scale
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DSdetach_scale(hid_t did, hid_t dsid, unsigned int idx);
functions.description: Detaches the specified dimension scale (dsid) from dimension idx of dataset did. Removes the corresponding entries from DIMENSION_LIST (on did) and REFERENCE_LIST (on the scale). If the scale is attached to multiple dimensions of the same dataset, only the specified association is removed.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier.
dsid must be a valid dataset identifier that is a Dimension Scale.
idx must refer to a valid dimension index of did.
An existing attachment between did[idx] and dsid must exist; otherwise the call fails.
Caller must check the herr_t return value for success/failure.

functions.name: H5DSset_scale
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DSset_scale(hid_t dsid, const char *dimname);
functions.description: Converts a dataset (dsid) into a Dimension Scale. Creates the CLASS attribute with value "DIMENSION_SCALE" and an empty REFERENCE_LIST attribute. If dimname is non-NULL, creates a NAME attribute with that value. Intended usage: after creating/populating a dataset, call this to mark it as a scale before attaching it to other datasets.
requirements: dsid must be a valid dataset identifier.
dsid must not already be a Dimension Scale.
dsid must not already have dimension scales attached to it (a Dimension Scale cannot have scales).
dimname may be NULL (indicating no name) or a valid null-terminated string if provided.
Caller must check the herr_t return value for success/failure.
It is not recommended to convert datasets created with the Table, Image, or Palette interfaces (they have different CLASS values).

functions.name: H5DSget_num_scales
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL int H5DSget_num_scales(hid_t did, unsigned int idx);
functions.description: Returns the number of Dimension Scales attached to dimension idx of dataset did. On error, returns a negative value.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier.
idx must refer to a valid dimension index of did (0-based, within rank).
Caller must handle negative return values as errors.

functions.name: H5DSset_label
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DSset_label(hid_t did, unsigned int idx, const char *label);
functions.description: Sets the label for dimension idx of dataset did (DIMENSION_LABELS attribute). Replaces any existing label value.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier.
idx must refer to a valid dimension index of did.
label must be a valid null-terminated string; bad arguments cause failure.
Caller must check the herr_t return value for success/failure.

functions.name: H5DSget_label
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL ssize_t H5DSget_label(hid_t did, unsigned int idx, char *label, size_t size);
functions.description: Retrieves the label for dimension idx of dataset did into the provided buffer. Returns the label length on success, zero if no label is set, or a negative value on failure. Up to size bytes are copied to label; longer labels are truncated.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier.
idx must refer to a valid dimension index of did.
If label is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes; up to size characters will be written (label may be truncated).
Caller must check the ssize_t return value: negative indicates failure; zero indicates no label; positive indicates the label length.
If the caller needs the full label without truncation, ensure the buffer is large enough; the interface does not specify a dedicated size-query pattern in this header.

functions.name: H5DSget_scale_name
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL ssize_t H5DSget_scale_name(hid_t did, char *name, size_t size);
functions.description: Retrieves the NAME attribute of a Dimension Scale (did) into the provided buffer. Returns the length of the name on success, zero if no name exists, or a negative value on failure. Supports a size-query pattern by calling with name == NULL to obtain the required size.
requirements: did must be a valid identifier for a Dimension Scale (created via H5DSset_scale).
If name is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes; up to size bytes (including the null terminator) may be written.

To query the required buffer size, call with name == NULL; the return value will be the size of the scale name. For a subsequent call, pass size as returned_length + 1 to accommodate the null terminator, otherwise the last character may be truncated.
Caller must check the ssize_t return value: negative indicates failure; zero indicates no name; positive indicates the name length.

functions.name: H5DSis_scale
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL htri_t H3DSis_scale(hid_t did);
functions.description: Determines whether the given dataset identifier refers to a Dimension Scale (i.e., has CLASS="DIMENSION_SCALE"). Returns a positive value for true, zero for false, or a negative value on error.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier.
Caller must interpret htri_t correctly: >0 means true, 0 means false, <0 means error.

functions.name: H5DSiterate_scales
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5DSiterate_scales(hid_t did, unsigned int dim, int *idx, H5DS_iterate_t visitor, void *visitor_data);
functions.description: Iterates over the scales attached to dimension dim of dataset did, invoking the user-supplied visitor for each. The visitor conforms to typedef herr_t (*H5DS_iterate_t)(hid_t dset, unsigned dim, hid_t scale, void *visitor_data). Iteration semantics: visitor returning 0 continues; positive short-circuits and returns that value; negative aborts and returns that value. If idx is non-NULL, it supplies the starting position and receives the next position to visit; if NULL, iteration starts at the first scale and cannot be resumed.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier.
dim must refer to a valid dimension index of did (0-based, within rank).
visitor must be a non-NULL function pointer of type H5DS_iterate_t (herr_t (*)(hid_t dset, unsigned dim, hid_t scale, void *visitor_data)).
If idx is non-NULL, on input it must contain the starting index; on output it is set to the next index to visit.
The set of attached scales for the given dimension must remain unchanged for the duration of the iteration; modifying membership during iteration yields undefined behavior.
Caller must check the herr_t return value; it will be 0 on full completion, or the last non-zero visitor return value on early exit.

functions.name: H5DSis_attached
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL htri_t H5DSis_attached(hid_t did, hid_t dsid, unsigned int idx);
functions.description: Reports whether the specified dimension scale (dsid) is currently attached to dimension idx of dataset did. Returns a positive value if attached, zero if not attached, or a negative value on error.
requirements: did must be a valid dataset identifier that is not a Dimension Scale.
dsid must be a valid dataset identifier that is a Dimension Scale.
idx must refer to a valid dimension index of did.
Caller must interpret htri_t correctly: >0 means attached, 0 means not attached, <0 means error.

functions.name: H5IMmake_image_8bit
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMmake_image_8bit(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hsize_t width, hsize_t height, const unsigned char *buffer);
functions.description: Creates and writes an indexed (8-bit) image dataset named dset_name under the file or group identified by loc_id. It tags the dataset with HDF5 Image/Palette attributes to mark it as an image. Pixel data are interpreted as H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR and written from buffer. Typical use: call to create an 8-bit image dataset of size width x height, then optionally attach palettes and/or read later.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier open in a state that allows dataset creation.
dset_name must be a non-null, null-terminated path/name valid in the target loc_id and not already used for an existing object at that path.
width and height must be positive (non-zero) image dimensions.
buffer must be non-null and contain at least width*height bytes of image data (H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR).
The dataset created is typed as native unsigned char per the HDF5 Image specification.
Any necessary intermediate groups for dset_name must exist or be created by the caller beforehand (not specified here).
Errors are reported via the herr_t return value (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMmake_image_24bit
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMmake_image_24bit(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hsize_t width, hsize_t height, const char *interlace, const unsigned char *buffer);
functions.description: Creates and writes a true-color (24-bit, RGB) image dataset named dset_name under loc_id. The image is marked with HDF5 Image/Palette attributes. Pixel data are H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR. The interlace parameter specifies how color components are laid out: INTERLACE_PIXEL or INTERLACE_PLANE per the HDF5 Image specification.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier open for dataset creation.
dset_name must be non-null, a valid path/name under loc_id, and not already used.
width and height must be positive (non-zero) image dimensions.
interlace must be a non-null string and one of the supported values: "INTERLACE_PIXEL" or "INTERLACE_PLANE" (per documentation).
buffer must be non-null and large enough for the image data layout implied by interlace (typically 3*width*height bytes for RGB).
Pixel type is H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR (caller must supply data in that type/size).
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMget_image_info
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMget_image_info(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hsize_t *width, hsize_t *height, hsize_t *planes, char *interlace, hssize_t *npals);
functions.description: Retrieves metadata about an image dataset dset_name under loc_id: its width, height, number of color planes, interlace mode string, and the number of associated palettes.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with read access to the dataset.
dset_name must be non-null and refer to an existing dataset that is an HDF5 Image per the Image/Palette specification.
width, height, planes, interlace, and npals pointers provided for output must be valid (non-null) for the fields the caller wishes to retrieve; any null pointer cannot be written.

The interlace output buffer must be large enough to hold the interlace mode string (e.g., "INTERLACE_PIXEL" or "INTERLACE_PLANE"); exact maximum length is not specified here (caller should allocate a sufficiently large buffer).
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMread_image
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMread_image(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, unsigned char *buffer);
functions.description: Reads the raw image data from the image dataset dset_name under loc_id into buffer. Intended for datasets created/marked as HDF5 Images.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with read access to the dataset.
dset_name must be non-null and refer to an existing image dataset.

buffer must be non-null and large enough to hold the entire dataset’s image data; the required size depends on the dataset (e.g., width*height for 8-bit indexed or 3*width*height for 24-bit RGB). Query with H5IMget_image_info first to size the buffer correctly.
The element type is unsigned char (H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR).
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMmake_palette
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMmake_palette(hid_t loc_id, const char *pal_name, const hsize_t *pal_dims, const unsigned char *pal_data);
functions.description: Creates and writes a palette dataset named pal_name under loc_id and tags it with HDF5 Image/Palette attributes to identify it as a palette. The palette data type is H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR. Typical usage: define pal_dims to the intended palette dimensions and supply pal_data accordingly.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier open for dataset creation.
pal_name must be non-null, a valid path/name, and not already used.

pal_dims must be a non-null pointer to an array of palette dimensions sized appropriately for the intended palette rank; the exact expected rank/length is defined by the HDF5 Image/Palette specification (not specified here).
pal_data must be non-null and contain at least the product of pal_dims elements as unsigned bytes (H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR).
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMlink_palette
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMlink_palette(hid_t loc_id, const char *image_name, const char *pal_name);
functions.description: Attaches an existing palette dataset pal_name to an image dataset image_name under loc_id. If the image already has palettes, the palette reference list is extended.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with write permission to modify attributes/links of the image dataset.
image_name must be non-null and refer to an existing image dataset under loc_id.
pal_name must be non-null and refer to an existing palette dataset under loc_id.
The function may extend the set of palette references attached to the image; caller should ensure palette indices remain valid for subsequent queries.
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMunlink_palette
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMunlink_palette(hid_t loc_id, const char *image_name, const char *pal_name);
functions.description: Detaches a palette named pal_name from the image dataset image_name under loc_id.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with write permission to modify the image’s palette associations.
image_name must be non-null and refer to an existing image dataset under loc_id.
pal_name must be non-null and refer to a palette currently attached to the image.
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMget_npalettes
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMget_npalettes(hid_t loc_id, const char *image_name, hssize_t *npals);
functions.description: Returns in npals the number of palettes associated with the image dataset image_name under loc_id.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with read access.
image_name must be non-null and refer to an existing image dataset.
npals must be non-null and point to writable memory.
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMget_palette_info
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMget_palette_info(hid_t loc_id, const char *image_name, int pal_number, hsize_t *pal_dims);
functions.description: Retrieves the dimensions of the palette dataset attached to image_name at zero-based index pal_number and writes them into pal_dims.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with read access.
image_name must be non-null and refer to an existing image dataset.
pal_number must be a zero-based index identifying an attached palette; it must be within [0, npals-1] where npals is obtained via H5IMget_npalettes.
pal_dims must be non-null and point to an array large enough to receive all palette dimensions; exact number of dimensions is defined by the HDF5 Image/Palette specification (not specified here).
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMget_palette
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMget_palette(hid_t loc_id, const char *image_name, int pal_number, unsigned char *pal_data);
functions.description: Reads the palette dataset attached to image_name at zero-based index pal_number into pal_data.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with read access.
image_name must be non-null and refer to an existing image dataset.
pal_number must be a zero-based index within the number of palettes attached to the image (0..npals-1).
pal_data must be non-null and large enough to hold the entire palette dataset; determine size from H5IMget_palette_info before calling.
Palette element type is unsigned char (H5T_NATIVE_UCHAR).
Errors are reported via herr_t (non-negative on success, negative on failure; standard HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5IMis_image
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMis_image(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name);
functions.description: Checks whether the dataset dset_name under loc_id is an HDF5 Image per the Image/Palette specification. Note: Documentation comments indicate a tri-state return type (htri_t), but this header declares herr_t; behavior should be confirmed against the library version in use.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with read access.
dset_name must be non-null and refer to an existing dataset path under loc_id.

Return type is herr_t as declared here; per standard HDF5 conventions, non-negative indicates success (with inquiry result possibly conveyed via value in implementations that use htri_t). Because of the doc/signature discrepancy, callers should verify expected semantics for their build of HDF5 HL.

functions.name: H5IMis_palette
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5IMis_palette(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name);
functions.description: Checks whether the dataset dset_name under loc_id is a palette dataset per the HDF5 Image/Palette specification. Note: Documentation comments indicate a tri-state return type (htri_t), but this header declares herr_t; confirm the actual return semantics for your build.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier with read access.
dset_name must be non-null and refer to an existing dataset path under loc_id.
Return type is herr_t as declared; standard HDF5 convention is non-negative on success and negative on failure, but documentation suggests an inquiry style return (htri_t). Verify for your version.

functions.name: H5LDget_dset_dims
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5LDget_dset_dims(hid_t did, hsize_t *cur_dims);
functions.description: Retrieves the current dimension sizes of the HDF5 dataset identified by did and writes them into the user-provided array cur_dims. Typical usage is to call this after opening a dataset to learn its current extent; failure is returned if cur_dims is NULL. The array must be large enough to hold the dataset’s rank number of dimensions.
requirements: did must be a valid, open HDF5 dataset identifier.
cur_dims must not be NULL (the function returns failure if cur_dims is NULL).
cur_dims must point to writable memory large enough to hold one hsize_t per dataset dimension (i.e., dataset rank).
Caller should check the herr_t return value: non-negative indicates success; negative indicates failure (HDF5 convention).
The dataset must have a simple dataspace with a defined rank (implied by needing dimension sizes).

functions.name: H5LDget_dset_type_size
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL size_t H5LDget_dset_type_size(hid_t did, const char *fields);
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the dataset’s datatype. If fields is NULL, returns the size of the dataset’s datatype. If the dataset has a compound datatype and fields is non-NULL, returns the size of the selected field(s) specified by a comma-separated list; nested fields are separated by dots, and backslashes escape separator characters in names. Returns 0 on failure.
requirements: did must be a valid, open HDF5 dataset identifier.
If fields is NULL, the function returns the size of the dataset’s datatype.
If fields is non-NULL, the dataset should have a compound datatype; fields must be a comma-separated list of field names, using '.' for nested fields and '\' to escape ',' or '.' in field names.
Caller must treat a return value of 0 as failure and a positive value as the size in bytes (per documentation).

functions.name: H5LDget_dset_elmts
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5LDget_dset_elmts(hid_t did, const hsize_t *prev_dims, const hsize_t *cur_dims, const char *fields, void *buf);
functions.description: Retrieves selected data from the dataset identified by did into buf. The selection is defined by the difference between prev_dims and cur_dims; cur_dims must have at least one dimension larger than the corresponding prev_dims, indicating newly appended/changed region to read. If fields is NULL, data for selected elements are returned. If fields is non-NULL and the dataset has a compound datatype, only the specified field(s) (comma-separated, with '.' for nested fields and '\' as escape) are read. The buffer must be large enough to hold the number of selected elements times the datatype (or selected fields) size.
requirements: did must be a valid, open HDF5 dataset identifier.
prev_dims must point to an array of dimension sizes corresponding to the dataset’s previous extent; must not be NULL (required to define the selection).
cur_dims must point to an array of the current dimension sizes; must not be NULL.
prev_dims and cur_dims must describe arrays of the same rank (implied by element-wise comparison).
cur_dims must have at least one dimension whose size is greater than the corresponding dimension in prev_dims (explicitly stated).

buf must point to writable memory large enough to hold all selected elements: datatype_size × number_of_selected_elements (explicitly stated). For compound selections, use the size of the selected field set.
If fields is non-NULL, the dataset should have a compound datatype; fields must be a comma-separated list of field names, using '.' for nested fields and '\' to escape separator characters.
Caller should determine datatype size via H5LDget_dset_type_size(did, fields) and compute the number of selected elements from prev_dims and cur_dims.
Caller should check the herr_t return value: non-negative indicates success; negative indicates failure (HDF5 convention).

functions.name: H5LTmake_dataset
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5LTmake_dataset(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, int rank, const hsize_t *dims, hid_t type_id, const void *buffer);
functions.description: Creates and writes a new dataset named dset_name at loc_id with the specified dataspace rank/dims and element datatype type_id; writes the provided buffer into the dataset. Typical use is to create a simple (contiguous) dataset in a group or file object without manually constructing dataspaces and datatypes.
requirements: loc_id must identify an existing HDF5 object (commonly a file or group) where the dataset will be created.
dset_name must be a valid, non-NULL path/name for the target container; if the dataset exists it may be overwritten by this high-level API (behavior implementation-defined).
rank must be >= 1 for array datasets; for scalars use rank==0 (if supported by implementation); must match dims length.
dims must be a valid pointer to an array of at least rank hsize_t elements; each dimension size should be >= 1 for non-scalar.
type_id must be a valid HDF5 datatype identifier (e.g., H5T_NATIVE_INT).
buffer must be non-NULL and contain at least the number of elements equal to the product of dims, each compatible with type_id.
Caller must check the herr_t return value for errors and handle failures.

requirements: text must be a non-NULL DDL-compliant description of an HDF5 datatype.
lang_type must be a supported language constant; currently H5LT_DDL.
Caller must check the returned hid_t: non-negative indicates success; negative indicates failure.
Caller is responsible for closing the returned datatype id when no longer needed.

functions.name: H5LTdtype_to_text
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5LTdtype_to_text(hid_t dtype, char *str, H5LT_lang_t lang_type, size_t *len);
functions.description: Converts an HDF5 datatype id to a textual description in the given language (currently DDL). If str is NULL, returns the required buffer size via len; otherwise writes into str (possibly truncated if len too small).
requirements: dtype must be a valid datatype identifier.
lang_type must be supported; currently H5LT_DDL.
If str is NULL, len must be non-NULL to receive required size; if str is non-NULL, len should point to available buffer size and will be updated per behavior described.
If str is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory of at least *len bytes to avoid truncation.
Check herr_t.

functions.name: H5LTfind_attribute
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5LTfind_attribute(hid_t loc_id, const char *name);
functions.description: Determines whether an attribute named name exists on the object identified by loc_id. Note: The comment block documents return type htri_t (TRUE/FALSE/neg on error), but header declares herr_t; behavior may map similarly.
requirements: loc_id must be an object identifier referring to the object to be checked.
name must be a non-NULL attribute name.
Caller must interpret return value per implementation; positive/zero/negative semantics are typical in HDF5 for tri-state results.
Check for negative return to detect errors.

functions.name: H5LTpath_valid
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL htri_t H5LTpath_valid(hid_t loc_id, const char *path, bool check_object_valid);
functions.description: Checks whether path is a valid HDF5 link path relative to loc_id and optionally whether it resolves to an existing object. Returns TRUE if valid (and, if requested, resolves to an object), FALSE otherwise; negative on error. Special behavior for "/" noted in docs (always positive for valid root).
requirements: loc_id must be an identifier for an object in the file (file/group recommended).
path must be a non-NULL HDF5 path string (absolute or relative); "." is allowed for the object itself.
If path is absolute, loc_id can be any object in the file; if relative, loc_id must be a file or group identifier.
check_object_valid controls whether to require the final component to resolve to an actual object (TRUE) or just validate links (FALSE).
Caller must handle tri-state return: >0 TRUE, 0 FALSE, <0 error.

functions.name: H5LTopen_file_image
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL hid_t H5LTopen_file_image(void *buf_ptr, size_t buf_size, unsigned flags);
functions.description: Opens an HDF5 file image that resides in memory at buf_ptr with size buf_size using the Core (H5FD_CORE) VFD, returning a file identifier. Flags control read/write mode and ownership/release behavior for the supplied buffer.
requirements: buf_ptr must be non-NULL (function fails if NULL).
buf_size must be > 0 (function fails if 0).
flags may include H5LT_FILE_IMAGE_OPEN_RW to allow read/write; otherwise the file image is opened read-only.
If using H5LT_FILE_IMAGE_DONT_COPY, HDF5 will use the provided buffer directly; otherwise the image may be copied internally.
H5LT_FILE_IMAGE_DONT_RELEASE is only valid when used together with H5LT_FILE_IMAGE_DONT_COPY; it instructs HDF5 not to free the user-supplied buffer at file close.
Caller must close the returned file identifier when done.
Caller must check for negative return value to detect failure.

functions.name: H5PTcreate
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL hid_t H5PTcreate(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hid_t dtype_id, hsize_t chunk_size, hid_t plist_id);
functions.description: Creates and opens a packet table named dset_name under the object identified by loc_id. The packet table stores fixed-length or variable-length packets described by dtype_id, uses chunked storage sized by chunk_size, and can be configured via plist_id (e.g., compression). The returned identifier must later be closed with H5PTclose().
requirements: loc_id must identify a valid HDF5 location (file or group) able to contain a dataset (inferred from HDF5 API patterns and docs).
dset_name must point to a valid, null-terminated name for the new packet table (inferred).
dtype_id must be a valid HDF5 datatype identifier; may be fixed- or variable-length; compound types may include variable-length fields (stated).
chunk_size is the number of table entries per chunk; affects performance (stated).
plist_id is a valid property list identifier appropriate for dataset creation and may specify compression (stated).
On success returns a valid packet table identifier; on error returns H5I_INVALID_HID; caller must check return value (stated).
The created packet table must be closed with H5PTclose() (stated).

functions.name: H5PTopen
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL hid_t H5PTopen(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name);
functions.description: Opens an existing packet table named dset_name located at loc_id (file or group). Works for both fixed- and variable-length packet tables. The returned identifier must be closed with H5PTclose().
requirements: loc_id must identify a valid HDF5 location (file or group) that contains the packet table (inferred from docs).
dset_name must be a valid, null-terminated name of an existing packet table at loc_id (inferred).
On success returns a valid packet table identifier; on error returns H5I_INVALID_HID; caller must check return value (stated).
The opened packet table must be closed with H5PTclose() (stated).

functions.name: H5PTclose
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTclose(hid_t table_id);
functions.description: Closes an open packet table identified by table_id and releases associated resources (including certain identifiers returned by H5PTget_dataset and H5PTget_type, per notes).
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table identifier (inferred).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on failure (HDF5 herr_t convention; inferred).
Must be called to end access to a packet table opened or created by H5PTopen/H5PTcreate (stated).

functions.name: H5PTcreate_fl
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL hid_t H5PTcreate_fl(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hid_t dtype_id, hsize_t chunk_size, int compression);
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates and opens a packet table for fixed-length packets (also documented as permitting variable-length datatypes) with chunked storage sized by chunk_size and a simple compression level. Use H5PTcreate() instead. The returned identifier must be closed with H5PTclose().
requirements: loc_id must identify a valid HDF5 location (file or group) able to contain the dataset (inferred).
dset_name must be a valid, null-terminated name for the new packet table (inferred).
dtype_id must be a valid HDF5 datatype identifier; may include variable-length fields (stated).
chunk_size is the number of table entries per chunk; affects performance (stated).
compression is a compression level: 0..9; -1 indicates no compression (stated).
On success returns a valid packet table identifier; on error returns H5I_INVALID_HID; caller must check return value (stated).
Must be closed with H5PTclose() (stated).

functions.name: H5PTappend
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTappend(hid_t table_id, size_t nrecords, const void *data);
functions.description: Appends nrecords packets to the end of the packet table identified by table_id. For fixed-length tables, data points to nrecords of the table’s element type; for variable-length tables, data points to nrecords of hvl_t structs.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
data must point to a buffer containing at least nrecords packets of the appropriate element representation (stated).
For variable-length packet tables, data must be an array of hvl_t values (stated).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5PTget_next
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTget_next(hid_t table_id, size_t nrecords, void *data);
functions.description: Reads nrecords packets starting from the packet table’s current index into data, then advances the internal index accordingly. For variable-length tables, the elements read are hvl_t entries and the allocated memory must later be released with H5PTfree_vlen_buff().
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
Before first use after create/open, the table’s index should be initialized with H5PTcreate_index() or set with H5PTset_index() (stated).
data must point to writable storage sufficient for nrecords packets of the table’s element representation (stated/inferred).
For variable-length packet tables, the returned data elements are hvl_t and the allocated memory must be freed by calling H5PTfree_vlen_buff() (stated).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5PTread_packets
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTread_packets(hid_t table_id, hsize_t start, size_t nrecords, void *data);
functions.description: Reads nrecords packets starting at packet index start from the packet table identified by table_id into data. For variable-length tables, the elements read are hvl_t entries and the allocated memory must later be released with H5PTfree_vlen_buff().
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
start indicates the zero-based packet index at which to begin reading (inferred from docs; zero-index implied elsewhere).
data must point to writable storage sufficient for nrecords packets of the table’s element representation (stated/inferred).
For variable-length packet tables, the returned data elements are hvl_t and the allocated memory must be freed by calling H5PTfree_vlen_buff() (stated).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5PTget_num_packets
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTget_num_packets(hid_t table_id, hsize_t *nrecords);
functions.description: Retrieves the number of packets currently stored in the packet table identified by table_id and writes it to *nrecords.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
nrecords must be a non-NULL pointer to writable hsize_t storage (inferred).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5PTis_valid
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTis_valid(hid_t table_id);
functions.description: Checks whether table_id refers to an open packet table. Returns a non-negative value if valid, negative otherwise.
requirements: table_id can be any identifier; function determines if it is a packet table (stated).
Caller must interpret a non-negative return as valid and a negative return as invalid/error (stated).

functions.name: H5PTis_varlen
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTis_varlen(hid_t table_id);
functions.description: Determines whether the packet table identified by table_id stores variable-length or fixed-length packets. Returns 1 for variable-length, 0 for fixed-length, or a negative value if table_id is not a packet table or on error.
requirements: table_id must be an identifier to query (stated).
Caller must handle three outcomes: 1 (variable-length), 0 (fixed-length), negative (error/not a packet table) (stated).

functions.name: H5PTget_dataset
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL hid_t H5PTget_dataset(hid_t table_id);
functions.description: Returns the dataset identifier underlying the packet table identified by table_id. The returned dataset identifier will be closed by H5PTclose() and should not be closed separately by the caller.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
On success returns a dataset identifier; on error returns H5I_INVALID_HID; caller must check (stated).
The returned dataset identifier will be closed when H5PTclose() is called on the packet table; callers should not close it independently to avoid double-close (stated).

functions.name: H5PTget_type
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL hid_t H5PTget_type(hid_t table_id);
functions.description: Returns the datatype identifier used by the packet table identified by table_id. The returned datatype identifier will be closed by H5PTclose() and should not be closed separately by the caller.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
On success returns a datatype identifier; on error returns H5I_INVALID_HID; caller must check (stated).
The returned datatype identifier will be closed when H5PTclose() is called on the packet table; callers should not close it independently (stated).

functions.name: H5PTcreate_index
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTcreate_index(hid_t table_id);
functions.description: Initializes or resets the packet table’s internal ‘current index’ to the first packet so H5PTget_next() can iterate from the beginning. Must be called after create/open (or after closing/reopening) before using H5PTget_next() unless H5PTset_index() is used instead.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
Should be called each time a packet table is created or opened before using H5PTget_next() (stated).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5PTset_index
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTset_index(hid_t table_id, hsize_t pt_index);
functions.description: Sets the packet table’s current index to pt_index (packets are zero-indexed) so that subsequent H5PTget_next() reads proceed from that position.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
pt_index is zero-based and should refer to a valid packet position (stated/inferred).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5PTget_index
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTget_index(hid_t table_id, hsize_t *pt_index);
functions.description: Retrieves the current record index for the packet table identified by table_id and writes it to *pt_index.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table (stated/inferred).
pt_index must be a non-NULL pointer to writable hsize_t storage (stated/inferred).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5PTfree_vlen_buff
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5PTfree_vlen_buff(hid_t table_id, size_t bufflen, void *buff);
functions.description: Frees memory that was automatically allocated when reading variable-length packets from the packet table identified by table_id. Call this after reading variable-length data (via H5PTget_next or H5PTread_packets) into buff to release all allocated memory.
requirements: table_id must be a valid open packet table from which the variable-length packets in buff were read (stated/inferred).
buff must be the same buffer that received the variable-length packet data (stated).
bufflen must describe the size/length of buff as used in the read operation (stated).
Must be called to release memory after reading variable-length packets; not required for fixed-length packets (stated).
Returns non-negative on success and negative on error; caller must check (herr_t convention; stated).

functions.name: H5TBmake_table
functions.description: Creates and writes an HDF5 dataset intended to be interpreted as a table. It defines a compound datatype with named fields and writes nrecords of data from buf into a new dataset dset_name under loc_id. Use when first creating a table-like dataset with fixed-length fields; supports optional chunking, compression, and per-field fill values.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be a valid, null-terminated name for the dataset to create and must not already conflict per HDF5 rules.
nfields must match the number of entries in field_names[], field_offset, and field_types arrays.
type_size must be the sizeof() of the C struct representing one record.
field_names[] must contain nfields null-terminated field names.
field_offset must point to an array of length nfields with byte offsets for each field (e.g., computed with HOFFSET).
field_types must point to an array of length nfields with valid HDF5 datatype identifiers for each field.
nrecords specifies the number of records to create and write from buf; if nrecords > 0, buf must point to at least nrecords records of size type_size.
chunk_size specifies the dataset chunk size; usage beyond that is unspecified here.
fill_data, if non-NULL, must point to per-field fill value data laid out according to the record type; if NULL, default fill behavior applies.
compress is a flag to toggle compression (0 disables, nonzero enables).
On error, the function returns a negative herr_t; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: H5TBappend_records
functions.signature:
H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBappend_records(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hsize_t nrecords, size_t type_size,
                                   const size_t *field_offset, const size_t *dst_sizes, const void *buf);
functions.description: Appends records to the end of an existing table dataset dset_name under loc_id, extending the dataset to accommodate the additional rows. Data is taken from buf and interpreted according to the provided struct layout.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be a valid, existing table dataset name under loc_id.
nrecords is the number of records to append; if nrecords > 0, buf must point to at least nrecords records.
type_size must be the sizeof() of the C struct representing one record.
field_offset must point to an array of per-field byte offsets for the table’s schema (computed with HOFFSET).
dst_sizes must point to an array of per-field sizes (in bytes) for the table’s schema.
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0 and laid out as nrecords contiguous records of size type_size.
Returns negative herr_t on error; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: H5TBwrite_records
functions.description: Overwrites nrecords records starting at zero-based index start in the table dataset dset_name under loc_id. The dataset must already exist; data is taken from buf according to the given struct layout.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
start is the zero-based starting record index to overwrite; must be within the dataset’s current extent so that the range [start, start + nrecords) is valid.
nrecords is the number of records to write; if nrecords > 0, buf must contain that many records.
type_size must be sizeof(record struct).
field_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets (compatible with the dataset’s schema).
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field sizes in bytes (compatible with the dataset’s schema).
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0.
Check the herr_t return value for errors (negative indicates failure).

functions.name: H5TBwrite_fields_name
functions.description: Overwrites one or more fields in existing records of table dset_name under loc_id, selecting fields by name(s). field_names identifies the field(s) to write (commonly a name or a delimiter-separated list, per HDF5 HL conventions). Writes nrecords starting at zero-based record index start using data from buf laid out per the provided struct layout.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
field_names must be a valid string identifying one or several fields; exact formatting (e.g., delimiter) follows the library’s conventions (not fully specified here).
start is the zero-based starting record index; [start, start + nrecords) must be within the dataset’s extent.
nrecords is the number of records to write; if nrecords > 0, buf must contain that many records.
type_size must be sizeof(record struct).
field_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets corresponding to the struct layout.
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field sizes in bytes corresponding to the struct layout.
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0.
Callers must check herr_t return for errors.

functions.name: H5TBwrite_fields_index
functions.description: Overwrites one or multiple fields selected by index in existing records of table dset_name under loc_id. field_index lists the zero-based field positions to update; nfields is its length. Writes nrecords starting at start using buf and the provided struct layout.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
nfields specifies the number of fields to overwrite and must match the length of field_index.
field_index must point to an array of nfields valid field indices for the dataset’s schema.
start is the zero-based starting record index; [start, start + nrecords) must be valid.
nrecords is the number of records to write; if nrecords > 0, buf must contain that many records.
type_size must be sizeof(record struct).
field_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets for the struct layout.
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field sizes in bytes for the struct layout.
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0.
Check herr_t return value for failure (negative).

functions.name: H5TBread_table
functions.signature:
H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBread_table(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, size_t dst_size, const size_t *dst_offset,
                               const size_t *dst_sizes, void *dst_buf);
functions.description: Reads all records from the table dataset dset_name under loc_id into dst_buf using the caller’s struct layout (dst_size, dst_offset, dst_sizes). Use to bulk-read the entire table.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
dst_size must be sizeof(destination record struct).
dst_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets (computed with HOFFSET) matching the destination struct.
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field sizes in bytes for the destination struct.
dst_buf must be non-NULL and large enough to hold all records in the table (table_nrecords * dst_size).
Callers must check the herr_t return (negative on error).

functions.name: H5TBread_fields_name
functions.description: Reads one or more fields identified by name(s) from table dset_name under loc_id into buf. Reads nrecords starting at start, mapping into the caller’s struct layout (type_size, field_offset, dst_sizes).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
field_names must be a valid string identifying the field(s) to read; exact formatting is library-defined (not fully specified here).
start is the starting record index to read from; must be within the dataset’s extent, and the range [start, start + nrecords) must be valid.
nrecords is the number of records to read; if nrecords > 0, buf must have storage for that many records of size type_size.
type_size must be sizeof(destination record struct).
field_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets for the destination struct.
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field sizes in bytes for the destination struct.
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0.
Negative herr_t return indicates error; callers must check.

functions.name: H5TBread_fields_index
functions.description: Reads one or more fields selected by index from table dset_name under loc_id into buf. field_index lists the zero-based field indices to read; nfields is its length. Reads nrecords starting at start into caller’s struct layout.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
nfields must equal the length of field_index.
field_index must be an array of valid field indices for the dataset schema.
start is the starting record index; [start, start + nrecords) must be valid.
nrecords is the number of records to read; buf must hold nrecords records of size type_size when nrecords > 0.
type_size must be sizeof(destination record struct).
field_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets for the destination struct.
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field byte sizes for the destination struct.
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0.
Check herr_t return for errors.

functions.name: H5TBread_records
functions.description: Reads nrecords records starting at zero-based index start from the table dataset dset_name under loc_id into buf, mapping into the caller’s struct layout (dst_offset, dst_sizes).
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
start is the starting record index; the range [start, start + nrecords) must be valid.
nrecords is the number of records to read; buf must be large enough for nrecords records of size type_size when nrecords > 0.
type_size must be sizeof(destination record struct).
dst_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets for the destination struct (computed with HOFFSET).
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field sizes in bytes for the destination struct.
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0.
Negative herr_t indicates error; callers must check.

functions.name: H5TBget_table_info
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBget_table_info(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hsize_t *nfields, hsize_t *nrecords);
functions.description: Retrieves the number of fields (columns) and records (rows) for the table dataset dset_name under loc_id.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
nfields must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of fields.
nrecords must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of records.
Check herr_t return value; negative indicates failure.

functions.name: H5TBget_field_info
functions.signature:
H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBget_field_info(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, char *field_names[],
                                   size_t *field_sizes, size_t *field_offsets, size_t *type_size);
functions.description: Obtains field metadata for the table dataset dset_name under loc_id, including per-field names, sizes, offsets, and the total compound type size for a record.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.

field_names[] must be an array of pointers large enough to hold all field name strings; each entry must point to caller-allocated storage sufficient for the corresponding name (exact allocation requirements not specified here).
field_sizes must be a non-NULL array to receive per-field sizes (bytes).
field_offsets must be a non-NULL array to receive per-field byte offsets.
type_size must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the size in bytes of the HDF5 compound datatype representing a record.
Callers must check herr_t return for errors.

functions.name: H5TBdelete_record
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBdelete_record(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hsize_t start, hsize_t nrecords);
functions.description: Deletes nrecords records starting at zero-based index start from the middle of table dset_name under loc_id, shifting subsequent records up.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
start is the starting record index to delete from; [start, start + nrecords) must be within the table’s current extent.
nrecords is the number of records to delete; must be non-negative and not exceed the number of available records from start.
Check herr_t return for errors.

functions.name: H5TBinsert_record
functions.description: Inserts nrecords records at position start in table dset_name under loc_id, shifting existing records down. Record data is taken from buf using the provided struct layout.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
start is the zero-based insertion position; must be within [0, current_nrecords].
nrecords is the number of records to insert; if nrecords > 0, buf must provide nrecords records of size dst_size.
dst_size must be sizeof(record struct).
dst_offset must be an array of per-field byte offsets for the record struct.
dst_sizes must be an array of per-field sizes in bytes for the record struct.
buf must be non-NULL when nrecords > 0.
Check herr_t return value for errors.

functions.name: H5TBadd_records_from
functions.signature:
H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBadd_records_from(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name1, hsize_t start1, hsize_t nrecords,
                                     const char *dset_name2, hsize_t start2);
functions.description: Copies nrecords records starting at start1 from table dset_name1 to table dset_name2 at position start2. Both tables are attached to the same loc_id. Use to move or duplicate a range of rows between two tables with compatible schemas.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier common to both tables.
dset_name1 must be the name of an existing source table under loc_id.
start1 is the starting source record index; [start1, start1 + nrecords) must be valid in the source table.
nrecords is the number of records to copy; must not exceed the source’s available records.
dset_name2 must be the name of an existing destination table under loc_id.
start2 is the zero-based position in the destination table where records will be written/inserted; must be within the destination’s valid range.
Source and destination tables must have compatible schemas (implied by operation; exact constraints not specified here).
Check herr_t return value; negative indicates failure.

functions.name: H5TBcombine_tables
functions.signature:
H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBcombine_tables(hid_t loc_id1, const char *dset_name1, hid_t loc_id2,
                                   const char *dset_name2, const char *dset_name3);
functions.description: Combines records from two existing tables (dset_name1 under loc_id1 and dset_name2 under loc_id2) into a new table named dset_name3. The new table is created in the first file/group (loc_id1). Use to merge two tables (e.g., concatenation) into a newly created dataset.
requirements: loc_id1 and loc_id2 must be valid HDF5 file or group identifiers for the locations of the first and second tables, respectively (they may be the same).
dset_name1 and dset_name2 must be names of existing table datasets under loc_id1 and loc_id2, respectively.
dset_name3 must be a valid name for the new table to create; it will be written under loc_id1.
The two source tables must be combinable; schema compatibility is required but exact details are not specified here.
Callers must check herr_t return (negative on error).

functions.name: H5TBinsert_field
functions.signature:
H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBinsert_field(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, const char *field_name,
                                 hid_t field_type, hsize_t position, const void *fill_data, const void *buf);
functions.description: Inserts a new column (field) named field_name at zero-based index position into the table dset_name under loc_id. The operation rebuilds the table (re-creates and rewrites it) and can be expensive; optional fill_data provides per-field fill value for existing rows, and buf supplies the field data to write.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
field_name must be a valid, null-terminated field name not already present (implied by insert semantics; exact uniqueness rules not specified).
field_type must be a valid HDF5 datatype identifier for the new field.
position is the zero-based field index at which to insert; must be within [0, current_nfields].
fill_data may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to appropriate fill value data for the new field.
buf must point to data to be written for the new field across records; layout expectations are per library and not fully specified here.
Operation may leave unused space in the file and can take significant time for large tables (note).
Check herr_t return value for errors.

functions.name: H5TBdelete_field
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBdelete_field(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, const char *field_name);
functions.description: Deletes the field (column) named field_name from the table dset_name under loc_id. The table is re-created and rewritten; this can be expensive and may leave unused space in the file.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier.
dset_name must be an existing table dataset name.
field_name must be the name of an existing field in the table.
Operation re-creates and rewrites the table; callers should expect high cost for large tables.
Callers must check herr_t return (negative indicates failure).

functions.name: H5TBAget_title
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL herr_t H5TBAget_title(hid_t loc_id, char *table_title);
functions.description: Retrieves the title of the table identified by loc_id into table_title. Intended to read a table’s title attribute. Usage is to provide a buffer that will receive the title string.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier referencing the table for which to get the title (exact identification context not fully specified).
table_title must be a non-NULL caller-provided buffer large enough to store the table title, including the terminating null character (maximum size not specified here).
Callers must check herr_t return for errors.

functions.name: H5TBAget_fill
functions.signature: H5HL_DLL htri_t H5TBAget_fill(hid_t loc_id, const char *dset_name, hid_t dset_id, unsigned char *dst_buf);
functions.description: Reads the table attribute fill values for table dset_name (identified by loc_id and dset_id) into dst_buf. Returns 1 if a fill value is present, 0 if not present, and a negative value on error.
requirements: loc_id must be a valid HDF5 file or group identifier where the table resides.
dset_name must be the name of the target table.
dset_id must be a valid dataset identifier for the table.
dst_buf must be a non-NULL buffer large enough to hold the fill values for all table fields (exact size not specified here).
Callers must check the htri_t return value: 1 indicates presence, 0 indicates absence, negative indicates error.
